articles.title: Dubois vs Wardley 2: British heavyweights weigh in at career heaviest for world-title rematch
articles.summary: Britons Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley both weigh in at their career-heaviest for Saturday's heavyweight world-title rematch in London.
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley both weighed in at their career-heaviest and promised another explosive encounter in Saturday's heavyweight world-title rematch in London.

WBO champion Dubois tipped the scales at 18st 2lb (115kg) while Wardley came in at 17st 10lb (112kg) before their meeting at the O2 Arena.

The British rivals produced a fight-of-the-year contender in Manchester in May , with Wardley flooring Dubois twice before the Londoner rallied to stop his bloodied and battered opponent in the 11th round.

"I draw confidence from the successes I had in the first fight - getting knockdowns in the first and third," Wardley, 31, said.

"I need to capitalise on those moments better. I'm ready to put on a cleaner performance."

Dubois, 29, is more than 2lb heavier for the rematch, while Wardley has added more than 6lb.

Asked for his prediction, Wardley added: "Revenge, Fabio Wardley, knockout win."

Dubois v Wardley 2 - blood, bravery & a heavyweight gamble

Dubois v Wardley 2 - all you need to know

The final pre-fight formalities took place at Old Spitalfields Market in east London, with the two heavyweights taking to the scales amid the bustle of street-food stalls and shoppers.

A couple of hundred fans gathered beneath the market's Victorian roof, some having made the trip specifically for the event while others stopped to see what the fuss was about.

It was a rather subdued affair, with a smaller turnout than when Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic weighed in at the same venue in August.

Wardley arrived more than an hour before the event, appearing as relaxed as he has throughout fight week and even stopping for selfies with supporters afterwards.

Dubois arrived much later and has appeared in little mood for conversation this week. Once again, he was typically economical with his words.

"I know him now and know what to expect. I'm ready to go and do my job," the Londoner said. "I'm ready for a tear up. Let's go."

There was no drama at the obligatory face-off, despite the fierce rivalry that has developed between them, and two-time world champion Dubois was quick to leave the stage afterwards.

With 41 knockouts between them from 43 victories, few expect the contest to go the distance.

Wardley, sporting Ipswich Town's newly-launched third kit with his name printed on the sleeve, was still bearing the scars of his punishing defeat in Manchester five months ago.

A cut across the bridge of his nose, first sustained during his 2024 draw with Frazer Clarke, reopened against Dubois and left his face badly swollen and bloodied.

The punishment he absorbed has raised questions over whether his decision to take an immediate rematch has come too soon but Wardley remains confident he can reverse the result.

"It's simply seek and destroy now," he said.

Promoter Frank Warren is predicting a "blockbuster" 2027 for the heavyweight division, with lucrative fights awaiting Saturday's winner.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally meet in Cardiff on 11 December, while British prospect Itauma is set to return in January following his world-title defeat by Hrgovic.

Warren confirmed there is no clause for a third fight between Dubois and Wardley but the Queensberry Promotions boss refused to rule out a trilogy if the Ipswich fighter avenges the only defeat on his record.

"If that happens it's a natural fight," Warren said. "That's what's so intriguing about this. Who will they fight next year? We want to find out who is the best."

articles.title: Sean Strickland faces tense Edmonton confrontation after filming people, with angry stranger warning ‘you’ll get killed’
articles.summary: UFC fighter Sean Strickland found himself in a tense situation in downtown Edmonton, Canada, after a person confronted him for filming people on the
articles.body: UFC fighter Sean Strickland found himself in a tense situation in downtown Edmonton, Canada, after a person confronted him for filming people on the street. Strickland was in the city ahead of UFC Edmonton on October 17, 2026, to support teammate Melissa Croden, who is set to fight Chelsea Chandler. During his walk, he recorded videos showing people experiencing homelessness and what he described as open drug use. One person then approached him angrily and chased him as he tried to leave.Sean Strickland Faces Angry Confrontation After Recording People in EdmontonSean Strickland shared videos of his walk through downtown Edmonton on social media. In the clips, he showed people sitting or lying on the streets. He also claimed that drug use was taking place openly in the area.In one post, Strickland called the people he filmed “The free folk of Alberta.” He also gave one person his coffee. In another video, he described the scene as an “open dr*g market with zero police.”However, the situation took a different turn when a person noticed that Strickland was recording. The person became angry and warned him about filming people without asking them first.“When you do that kind of sh*t, ask permission for real, man. That will get you killed out here for real. I’m serious!” the person shouted in a video shared on X.Strickland tried to calm the person down. He replied, “It’s me. I’m recording me. It’s not you guys.”That explanation did not settle the argument. As the person moved closer, Strickland lowered his phone and tried to get away. The person then chased him down the street, but Strickland managed to escape.After reaching safety, the UFC fighter appeared to laugh about what had happened. He later posted the clip on X with the caption, “Id like to file a police report.”Strickland also joked about how dangerous the encounter felt, saying, “Bull sh*t. I almost died.”There were no reports of injuries from the incident. Still, the video showed how quickly a street recording can turn into a confrontation when the people being filmed do not want to be on camera.Sean Strickland Calls Alberta a “Trash Can” After Criticizing Conditions in EdmontonThe confrontation was not the only thing Strickland spoke about during his visit to Canada. The fighter also criticized the conditions he saw in Edmonton and questioned the police response to the problems on the streets.After leaving downtown, Strickland posted on X, “Left downtown and yep this place is a trash can.” He added, “Zombies everywhere.”He also shared another video showing a person lying still behind a fence. Strickland wrote that he was “pretty confident this man is dead or least freshly assaulted.” However, his post did not confirm whether the person was dead or had been assaulted.Strickland has criticized Canada before. During UFC 297 fight week in January 2024, he clashed with a reporter over questions about his views. The exchange drew attention and prompted UFC president Dana White to comment.The fighter has also spoken about a previous encounter with a homeless man in the United States. During a July 2026 appearance on Sean Ryan’s show, Strickland said the man had thrown a bicycle at his car. He claimed he then held the man at gunpoint until police arrived.His latest encounter in Edmonton adds to that history of tense interactions. articles.title: Mike Tyson’s son Amir Tyson pulls out of December boxing debut after trainer’s death, shifts fight to US
articles.summary: Mike Tyson’s son, Amir Tyson, will have to wait longer to make his boxing debut after the death of his trainer.
articles.body: Mike Tyson’s son, Amir Tyson, will have to wait longer to make his boxing debut after the death of his trainer. The 29-year-old was expected to fight at Misfits Boxing’s December 2026 event in England, but his plans have now changed. According to a deleted Instagram story shared by IFN Boxing, Amir said his debut had been moved to February 2027 in the United States. The delay comes as Amir deals with the loss of someone who was helping him prepare for his first fight in the ring.Amir Tyson Moves His Misfits Boxing Debut to February 2027 After Trainer’s DeathAmir Tyson shared the news in an Instagram story that was later posted by IFN Boxing on X. He explained why he would not be fighting in December and confirmed that his debut would take place at a different event.“My trainer died, so my fight is postponed from December to February now to get my head right, but it’s the States instead of England now,” Tyson wrote.Amir did not share his trainer’s name or explain when or how the death happened. He also did not reveal who he would face in his first fight. His message made it clear, however, that he needed more time before stepping into the ring.Misfits Boxing is scheduled to hold Misfits Mania 2 on December 5, 2026, in Manchester, England. The event has been linked to talks about a possible rematch between Jake Paul and Tommy Fury. Amir was expected to make his debut on the same card before his plans changed.Although his first opponent remains unknown, Amir has already shown interest in facing Misfits heavyweight champion Chase DeMoor. The two shared a heated faceoff in September. Amir said he wanted to win a few fights before challenging DeMoor for the heavyweight title.Misfits Boxing has not publicly announced its full plans for 2027. Amir’s post points to a February event in the United States, but further details about the show and his opponent have yet to be confirmed.Mike Tyson Warned Amir Tyson About the Pressure of Professional BoxingAmir’s decision to become a boxer comes despite his father’s earlier advice against it. Mike Tyson has spent years dealing with the demands of professional boxing and once explained why he did not want his son to follow the same path.During a 2021 episode of the Hotboxin’ with Mike Tyson podcast, the former heavyweight champion spoke about Amir’s interest in fighting Logan Paul and other influencer-boxers.“The oldest one, he’s 24, he wants to do this so bad,” Mike Tyson said. “He wants to fight Logan Paul and those guys. He wants to do that, but I said, ‘Just get a job. Get your real estate license. Just chill out, man. Why can’t you take advantage of your lightweight wealthiness? Just chill. You don’t want none of that heat, man, I’m telling you.’“This drives people to commit s***, getting humiliated in front of millions of people. You gotta be able to take that pressure and heat. Not many people can do it, man. It seems like a lot of people, but the people doing it is such a small percentage. It’s probably 1%, if that.”Mike’s main concern was the pressure fighters face when they compete in front of large audiences. He warned that public criticism and the risk of humiliation can be difficult to handle, even for people who are already famous.Before pursuing boxing, Amir worked as a media personality and was part of the broadcast team for his father’s 2024 fight against Jake Paul. He is now trying to build his own career in the sport.Despite his father’s concerns, Amir has chosen to move forward with boxing. His debut has been delayed, but his planned move to Misfits Boxing has not been reported as cancelled. articles.title: Lawrence Okolie hopes to resume boxing career after resolution with WBC following failed drug test this year
articles.summary: Lawrence Okolie failed an anti-doping test ahead of a fight against Tony Yoka in April; Okolie maintained his innocence in a statement on social media; British contender provided evidence that the adverse finding was the result of 'actions of a third party' without his knowledge
articles.body:
The British heavyweight returned an adverse analytical finding ahead of his scheduled fight against Tony Yoka in April, but Okolie maintained his innocence in a statement on social media.

Okolie had been the WBC No 1 ranked contender and the governing body held a review under their Clean Boxing Program, with the 33-year-old providing evidence that it was the 'result of the actions of a third party, without his knowledge or consent.'

A WBC statement read : "Throughout the process, Mr Okolie fully cooperated with the WBC's review and provided extenuating evidence supporting his position that the prohibited substance entered his system as a result of the actions of a third party, without his knowledge or consent.

"The WBC considered that mitigating evidence, together with Mr Okolie's unblemished testing history and cooperation throughout the process when reaching the agreed resolution.

Okolie, who had been in line for a WBC world heavyweight title shot, is now targeting a return to the ring.

"Clean sport has always been extremely important to me," he said in a statement. "I have cooperated fully throughout the process and remain committed to the highest standards of integrity in boxing. I look forward to the next chapter of my career and to being actively involved in the sport in the months ahead, while also using this experience to help educate other athletes about the importance of understanding and monitoring everything that enters their bodies."

WBC President Mauricio Sulaiman said: "The WBC Clean Boxing Program exists to protect athletes and the integrity of our sport. We appreciate Mr Okolie's cooperation throughout this process and welcome his commitment to helping educate fighters about anti-doping compliance and athlete responsibility."

As part of the agreed resolution, Okolie will remain available to undergo additional testing and to work with the WBC in support of education, awareness and compliance with anti-doping requirements among professional and amateur boxers.

articles.title: Figueroa loses title at weigh-in but Kameda can win it
articles.summary: Brandon Figueroa lost his World Boxing Association featherweight title on the scales Friday when the American failed to make weight for Saturday's bout again...
articles.body:
Brandon Figueroa lost his World Boxing Association featherweight title on the scales Friday when the American failed to make weight for Saturday's bout against Japan's Tomoki Kameda, organizers said.

The fight will be contested as scheduled in Las Vegas with Kameda able to take the crown with a victory and the title remaining vacant if Figueora wins.

Figueroa, a former super bantamweight world champion, enters the fight 27-2 with one drawn and 20 knockouts while Kameda is 42-5 with 23 knockouts.

Figueroa, 29, missed the 126-pound (57.1kg) weight limit by 1.4 pounds and surrenders the title he took from Britain's Nick Ball last February without ever defending it.

Kameda, 35, was the World Boxing Organization bantamweight champion in 2013 and 2014 and has not fought since May 2025 when he lost a title bout to International Boxing Federation champion Angelo Leo of the United States.

"It's disrespectful," Kameda said through a translator. "I suffered too. I did my thing. I'm ready for tomorrow. It has been 18 months since I fought. Look how shredded I am. I'm ready.

"The strategy remains the same. I'm going for the title."

articles.title: Raul Rosas Jr. debut, UFC-Bellator champs match added to RAF 15 lineup
articles.summary: The RAF 15 lineup in Chicago is filling up with a host of notable MMA names, including a matchup of former UFC and Bellator champions.
articles.body:
A notable UFC fighter's debut and a match pitting former UFC and Bellator champions highlight the latest additions to RAF 15.

On Friday, Real American Freestyle announced that rising UFC bantamweight Raul Rosas Jr. will step on the mat for the first time to meet UFC veteran Clay Guida, as well as a matchup of ex-UFC champ Cody Garbrandt taking on ex-Bellator champ Sergio Pettis.

RAF 15 takes place Nov. 28 in Chicago and streams live on Fox Nation.

Rosas Jr.'s booking comes just a few weeks after his knockout win over Raoni Barcelos in the UFC Fight Night 289 headliner. The fight-ending sequence was a scary scene as Barcelos apparently lost consciousness on a routine takedown by Rosas Jr.

No headliner for RAF 15 formally has been announced, although the promotion previously announced a matchup between Donald Cerrone and Anthony Pettis .

articles.title: Kamaru Usman Supports Sean Strickland in UFC Pay Dispute
articles.summary: UFC welterweight champion Kamaru Usman says that he supports UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland in his pay dispute with the promotion. Strickland is c...
articles.body:
UFC welterweight champion Kamaru Usman says that he supports UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland in his pay dispute with the promotion.

Strickland is currently involved in a back-and-forth pay dispute with the world's leading MMA promotion, as the UFC middleweight champ wants to make more money for his next title defense against Nassourdine Imavov, which is holding up the rematch between the two rivals.

For Usman, he supports Strickland's desire to hold out and get more money from the UFC.

Speaking on the "Pound 4 Pound" podcast, Usman revealed that he supports Strickland's quest to get a pay raise.

"It's a very difficult position and if you feel that you're not getting your just due, it doesn't matter. You're always going to want that. That's always going to supersede everything. So it doesn't matter if the noble thing to do here is to shut up and fight these fights out. No," Usman said (via MMAjunkie.com ).

"If you feel like you're not getting your just due, you're always going to say something. You're always going to feel some type of way. So yes, there's points on both sides, but it is what it is. It's a sucky situation, and this has been happening for a long, long time, and here we are – still happening. So Sean's not wrong for feeling the way that he feels."

While Usman supports Strickland's pay bump quest, he also sees things from the UFC's perspective and understands that since Strickland just signed a new deal in May, the promotion doesn't have to pay him more money.

"We all know exactly how he's feeling because we've been through it. The world is just unfair. There's points on both ends, so this guy has a point in saying, 'You signed this deal. You should honor it or be a part of it,' but this other guy is not wrong for trying to get as much as he can from an unfair world that we are in. All in all, it's just a tough situation to be in," Usman said.

articles.title: AEW star PAC died of asthma attack, medical examiner rules
articles.summary: PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, has officially been deemed a natural death, with no foul play suspected.
articles.body:
Benjamin Satterley, the former pro-wrestling star who went by the ring name "PAC" in AEW, died of bronchial asthma, the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office has ruled.

His death has officially been deemed a natural death, with no foul play suspected.

The New York Post was first to report the news Friday.

Satterley, who also performed under the ring name "Neville" in WWE, shockingly passed away on Sept. 27 at the age of 40 , just one day after his final wrestling match at AEW All Out 2026. Satterley was discovered unconscious around 4 p.m. in a rental car outside of a restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, and ultimately pronounced dead on the scene .

According to a police incident report, Satterley's phone was routing a Google Maps path to Chicago's O'Hare Airport upon his discovery, and a woman who knew Satterley told authorities the wrestler was heading there after stopping at the restaurant for lunch.

Hailed as one of the most acclaimed high-flying workers of his generation, Satterley debuted as a professional wrestler in his native England in 2004, then joined WWE in 2012, becoming a two-time WWE Cruiserweight Champion, one-time NXT Champion and two-time NXT Tag-Team Champion during his six years with the company.

After parting ways with the WWE, Satterley became one of AEW's earliest major signings in 2019, where he remained for the next seven years. Satterley won several championships with AEW — he became the promotion's inaugural All-Atlantic Champion in 2022 and twice captured its World Trios Championship — and had the distinction of being the first wrestler in AEW history to hold two championships simultaneously.

articles.title: No pagues por la pelea del Canelo vs Mbilli: ¿Dónde ver en TV abierta?
articles.standfirst: Canelo enfrenta a Christian Mbilli el 31 de octubre en Arabia Saudita
articles.summary: Canelo enfrenta a Christian Mbilli el 31 de octubre en Arabia Saudita
articles.body: Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez ya tiene fecha y rival para su regreso al cuadrilátero. El mexicano se medirá a Christian Mbilli el sábado 31 de octubre en Riad, Arabia Saudita, en un combate en el que el francés defenderá por primera vez el título mundial de peso supermediano del Consejo Mundial de Boxeo. La noche promete ser exigente: Mbilli llega invicto y con un estilo de presión constante que obligará a Álvarez a mostrar su mejor versión. El jalisciense de 36 años no pelea desde septiembre de 2025, cuando cayó ante Terence Crawford en Las Vegas. Después de ese combate se sometió a una operación de codo izquierdo, completó su rehabilitación y montó un campamento riguroso en Valencia, España, alejado del bullicio, algo que no había hecho con tanta disciplina en el pasado. Será su pelea profesional número 69 y la oportunidad de recuperar uno de los cinturones que perdió en 2025. La cartelera se podrá seguir en México por TV Azteca, con la narración del Box Azteca Team. Canelo mantiene el contrato con Turki Alalshikh y volvió a elegir la capital saudí como sede. El combate se realizará en The Venue de Riad y forma parte de la cartelera “México contra el mundo”. Las hojas de vida son contrastantes. Canelo suma 68 combates, con 63 victorias (39 por nocaut), tres derrotas y dos empates. Mbilli, de 31 años, llega con 30 peleas: 29 triunfos (24 por la vía rápida) y un empate. El mexicano tiene el doble de experiencia y ha llenado estadios en Las Vegas, Houston y Guadalajara. El francés, por su parte, es un campeón invicto que busca dar el golpe más grande de su carrera. Canelo ya fue campeón indiscutido de las 168 libras y ha conquistado títulos en cuatro divisiones distintas. Recuperar el cinturón del CMB le permitiría volver a ser monarca mundial en la categoría donde construyó gran parte de su legado reciente. Después de la derrota ante Terence Crawford en septiembre de 2025, Canelo se sometió a una operación de codo izquierdo. Completó la rehabilitación y montó un campamento exigente en Valencia, España, lejos del ruido mediático. El propio Saúl ha dicho que se siente como de 26 años, pero con más experiencia, y que necesitará mucha estamina porque Mbilli avanza hacia adelante, lanza muchos golpes y es fuerte. Mbilli, de 31 años, tiene marca de 29-0-1 con 24 nocauts. Fue elevado a campeón pleno del CMB en enero de 2026 tras la renuncia de Crawford al título. Esta será su primera defensa y la oportunidad de dar la campanada ante uno de los boxeadores más importantes de la última década. La pelea ya tiene fecha, sede y canal. El 31 de octubre, Canelo regresa por el cetro supermediano del CMB y la afición mexicana podrá seguirlo en vivo y gratis.

articles.title: Benjamin Satterley, wrestler known as Pac, died of bronchial asthma
articles.summary: Benjamin Satterley, known to wrestling fans around the world as Pac, died last month of bronchial asthma, the medical examiner’s office in Cook County, Illinois, confirmed Friday.
articles.body: Benjamin Satterley, known to wrestling fans around the world as Pac, died last month of bronchial asthma, the medical examiner’s office in Cook County, Illinois, confirmed Friday. The manner of death was natural, the office said. Satterley, 40, died Sept. 27, just one day after having wrestled on All Elite Wrestling’s “All Out” pay-per-view. His death sent waves of shock and grief across the world of professional wrestling. The New York Post first reported the cause of death. He was found in Des Plaines, around 2 miles north of the Chicago O’Hare International Airport, the medical examiner’s office said at the time. Satterley came up through the British independent system before making the leap to Japan and the U.S. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, he became a highly influential figure known both for his hard-hitting style and breathtaking aerial abilities. He went on to earn global acclaim, wrestling for some of the top promotions in the world, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. Satterley adopted the moniker of “The Bastard” at AEW, and captivated fans and contemporaries with the speed, grace, precision and power through which he moved in the ring. On the microphone, his promos conveyed a no-nonsense intensity that equally gripped viewers. At a time when the fourth wall between fan and wrestler had long collapsed, Satterley rarely broke character. Yet, his death highlighted the humility and kindness behind “The Bastard” persona. “He was just so modest about how fascinating he was,” Marina Shafir, a fellow member of the Death Riders stable of which Satterley was a part, said at an indie show hours after his death. “I wouldn’t be here today if I didn’t share time and space with this man,” she said. Days after his death, AEW turned its weekly “Dynamite” show into an emotional tribute to its fallen star, nicknamed “The Man That Gravity Forgot.” “Whilst he will always have a legacy as one of the greatest wrestlers the U.K. has ever produced, we have been so glad to see so many wonderful tributes that acknowledged who Ben was as a person,” the Satterley family said in a statement read during the show. “He exemplified what it meant to be a decent human being, an honorable man with principles, who adored his family and his sausage dog son, Wolfie.” On Instagram, his wife, Natalie, thanked Satterley “for our beautiful life.” “We will try our hardest to get through this nightmare and look after each other as I know that’s what you would want,” she wrote, “but we will miss you every minute, of every hour, of every day.”

articles.title: PFL Chicago results: Jena Bishop stuns Liz Carmouche for flyweight title, Dakota Ditcheva demands next
articles.summary: Bishop avenged her loss to Carmouche to claim the vacant PFL flyweight belt. Afterward, Ditcheva called for her long-awaited title shot in February or March.
articles.body:
Jena Bishop avenged her loss to Liz Carmouche to claim the vacant PFL flyweight title in the main event of PFL Chicago on Friday at Wintrust Arena.

Immediately after the event, Bishop faced off with Dakota Ditcheva, who threw her name in the hat to face the winner of the championship clash after being given the all-clear to return to full contact training earlier this week.

Bishop (12-3) showed great grit to remain in the contest after encountering some early adversity in Friday's rematch.

She was hanging on for dear life at the end of the first round after being put down by a short hook from Carmouche (26-9).

Despite that, she rallied well in the second, taking Carmouche down only to lose the position due to her landing illegal shots to the back of the head. Bishop's momentum carried into the third; a well-timed trip led to her taking Camouche's back, with the veteran calling on all her savvy to survive a minute-long hand fight to finish out the round.

After dropping two consecutive frames, Carmouche reintroduced herself in the fourth by landing much cleaner shots in the striking exchanges. Although Bishop appeared to be a spent force in the early exchanges of the final round, a scramble led to her taking Carmouche's back, where she threatened with a number of submission attempts before the bout ended.

"I thought it was either going to be really easy or it would be really tough, and I was prepared for it either way," Bishop said post-fight.

"I knew this was going to happen and I knew I was coming home with this belt."

Speaking on the broadcast earlier in the night, Ditcheva (16-0) revealed that she's been green lit for full-contact training after breaking both of her hands in her last outing, a decision win over Denise Kieholtz in July .

"Now that I've been cleared, I want to be the next person to fight for [the belt]," said Ditcheva.

"I know everyone calls me a prima donna, but if I'm not next in line, I might kick up a fuss a little bit. But I kind of understand at the same time — I do keep injuring myself."

"I'm ready to go, February or March I would love to get in and challenge someone for the belt," she added.

In the night's co-main event, boos chorused around the venue when Timur Khizriev (19-0) was announced the split decision victor of his rematch with Gabriel Braga (17-4).

Khizriev competed for the first time since he was shot five times by two masked attackers in Makhachkala, Dagestan in July 2025. That incident took place eight months after his last professional outing in November 2024, when he won the PFL featherweight tournament with a decision win over Brendan Loughnane.

He was dropped twice in the second round after being stunned by a stiff left hook by Braga in Friday's opening stanza. Although he matched Braga's volume, the Brazilian clearly landed the more damaging shots over the 15 minutes.

Braga cut a devastated figure when Khizriev was declared the winner, after appearing to be on the verge of putting the first blemish on Khizriev's undefeated record.

Earlier in the night, Sarvarjon Khamidov (18-1) made short work of Rafael do Nascimento (13-3) in their bantamweight clash.

The Brazilian was riding high on the back of his upset win over British prospect Lewis McGrillen, but was quickly brought crashing back to Earth when he met a thunderous Tajik hook before the two-minute mark of the first round.

articles.title: David Mora busca la redención en Georgia: "Van a ver algo a lo que no están acostumbrados"
articles.standfirst: El peleador madrileño debuta este sábado en Rkena ante el azerí Nabiev
articles.summary: El peleador madrileño debuta este sábado en Rkena ante el azerí Nabiev
articles.body: Rondan las 22.00 horas en Tiflis cuando David Mora (10-7) acaba el último entrenamiento del viernes en el piso 1 del hotel que Rkena ha elegido como base de operaciones en la capital de Georgia. El peleador del The Black Panther Gym madrileño cierra la activación previa al Fight Day, un calentamiento intenso para dormir a rienda suelta y llegar descansado al combate de este sábado ante el azerí Alim Nabiev (4-0). "Me encuentro muy bien, tengo muy buenas sensaciones", cuenta a MARCA David desde el hall de dicho hotel. El primer cara a cara con su rival tuvo lugar ayer, en el City Mall, después de cumplir con la báscula. 76,9 kilos para el español; 77,5 para el azerí. Un duelo en peso wélter que cerrará las preliminares del mayor evento de MMA realizado hasta la fecha en suelo georgiano. Ni el 4-0 (invicto) ni el bagaje de Nabiev, el 'Professor', en K1 o Kickboxing (ganó en Glory a Cédric Doumbé, por ejemplo), asustan a David Mora. Esto, como recuerda el español, son artes marciales mixtas. "Sabemos que viene de Glory, es puro striking. Sabemos que viene del kickboxing... y no es el MMA de ahora. Hay muchos movimientos a los que no está acostumbrado, está acostumbrado al guante grande, no le gusta mucho el contacto... la idea es ir acorralando. Veremos si lo llevamos arriba o nos vamos al suelo. Me gusta pegarme arriba pero también quiero mostrar mis habilidades, mi suelo, mi jiu jitsu… que por algo soy faixa preta también. No por haber peleado en Bare Knuckle solamente puedo combatir arriba, quiero mostrar mi abanico de habilidades. Quiero llevar a cabo mi juego", analiza. Un mensaje claro sobre lo que puede ser su 'game plan'. Para David Mora, ex campeón de AFL en España, este duelo en Georgia representa una gran oportunidad. Viene de dos derrotas consecutivas en MMA (WAR 2024, PFL 2026) y recuperar la actividad, algo que tiene en mente, pasa por salir victorioso este sábado en Tiflis. La velada, coordinada entre Rkena y PFL con la presencia de nombres como Aaron McKenzie, Ibragim Ibragimov o Abdul Kamara, es una buena oportunidad para volver a la órbita de la segunda mejor liga de MMA del mundo. "Una buena finalización, un buen show... me puede colocar en una buena posición para PFL Europa. Son todo ventajas para mí. Pero sobre todo disfrutar, ya lo difícil está hecho. Disfrutar del evento, del combate...", analiza Mora. A Tiflis, por ejemplo, más allá del equipo del Black Panther, se han desplazado dos seguidores desde Madrid para ver a David pelear. "No es ya por mí, es por la gente que me apoya desde el primer día. Hay gente que me sigue desde el día 1 de mi carrera. Hay dos chicos que han venido desde Madrid para verme pelear aquí en Georgia, eso me llena mucho. Que vengan aquí para verme... pues que menos que darle lo que se merecen. Mostrarles el show, acabar bien", dice, emocionado. Este sábado (desde las 14.00 hora española, cuando arranca la velada, se puede ver en YouTube gratis) será el momento de demostrarlo. "Van a ver algo a lo que no están acostumbrados", promete.

articles.title: Dubois vs Wardley 2 predictions for heavyweight WBO title fight from fighters and pundits
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's heavyweight world title rematch between Fabio Wardley and Daniel Dubois.
articles.body:
Five months after producing one of the most dramatic heavyweight fights of the year, Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley will renew their rivalry in London on Saturday.

Dubois, 29, makes the first defence of his WBO world title after climbing off the canvas twice to stop Wardley in the 11th round of their thrilling encounter in Manchester in May.

Ipswich's Wardley, 31, suffered the first defeat of his professional career that night but immediately activated his rematch clause in a bid to reclaim his world title.

With 41 knockouts between them in 43 combined victories, another explosive contest could be in store at the O2 Arena.

Can Dubois repeat his victory or will Wardley gain revenge and become a two-time world champion?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from across the boxing world to get their predictions.

Barry Jones - former super-featherweight world champion

"It's very hard to pick against the winner of the first fight when there's a rematch. Dubois was so composed, even after being knocked down twice. Wardley can knock out any person at any time, that's what took him from no experience on the white-collar scene to a world champion. You know what you will get with him.

"Dubois' issue has never been power, strength or bravery. It's when he has to think and can't find an answer and the panic occurs. If you whack him with big shots, he knows he can whack you back and hurt you.

"When he was knocked down, his corner played a great role to keep him calm and he knew what he had to do - hit Wardley clean and often.

"I think it will be the same result but Dubois might win a lot earlier this time. Wardley might knock him down and it will still be a thrilling fight while it lasts, but I think it will be Dubois inside five rounds."

"Repeat or revenge? I guess you have to go for repeat. Wardley had his moments in the first fight but Dubois was so dominant. Aside from the two knockdowns, Dubois was bullish, strong and aggressive. Getting up from those two knockdowns showed a lot as well.

"So I favour Dubois. We know Wardley has the knockout power but I think Dubois is the best heavyweight in the world - with Oleksandr Usyk on an island by himself and we'll wait to see what he will do next.

"Dubois is number one - with Wardley top five in the world - and I think he will take a lot of confidence knowing a) he is world champion and b) it's a very quick turnaround for Wardley who took a beating in the first fight five months ago.

"If I had to put money on someone, I'm putting all my chips on Dubois getting the stoppage again."

"It's a great fight. Credit to Wardley for going back in there after taking some serious, serious damage and still standing - unbelievable tenacity from the man. And he can hurt Dubois - we saw that in the first minute or so of the fight.

"For me, though, the smart money would be on another Dubois victory."

Richard Riakporhe - British heavyweight champion

"It's a fascinating fight. Dubois has tremendous power and is dangerous at any moment, but I slightly favour Wardley. I think his resilience, work rate and ability to find a way through tough moments could make the difference.

"I'd give Wardley a 60-40 edge, but I wouldn't be surprised either way."

Liam Gough – boxing content creator and BBC Sounds' Punch Perfect host

"I think Daniel Dubois will come into this fight with enormous confidence, particularly after the way he came through two early knockdowns and went on to dominate thereafter. I struggle to see what Fabio Wardley can do differently this time to change the outcome.

"I expect Dubois to be even more aggressive and menacing from the opening bell. His jab will be sharp, but what makes him so dangerous is that he has more than just a big right hand in his arsenal.

"Wardley is a huge puncher himself, but I believe Dubois has more dimensions to his game, with a Plan B and Plan C if things don't go exactly as planned. I don't think we're going to see a long feeling-out process here.

"Dubois will look to impose himself immediately, put Wardley under pressure and take control of the fight early. This could be explosive from the very first exchange, so don't blink - because I don't think this one is going to last very long."

Carl Frampton - former two-weight world champion

"I think it's going to be a repeat scenario, and it may even end earlier. I'm not trying to be disrespectful to Wardley but when you're involved in those types of fights and are on the end of a beating like he was, sometimes you're not the same when you come back.

"His nose doesn't look like it's recovered. The only way for Wardley to win is to throw the kitchen sink at Dubois for the first three or four rounds. That gives him a chance. But the longer it goes on, Dubois' jab will do damage and Wardley's nose will be damaged again.

"Wardley is extremely tough but that can sometimes be your downfall. We've seen it in the last fight and in his previous fights. He's been in some wars and that takes something away from you.

"I see Dubois winning between rounds seven and 10."

Emily Eubank - BBC Sounds' Punch Perfect host

"I'd love Fabio to level the score so we get a trilogy, and he certainly can, but it'll be a tough night's work. My head says Daniel will be too confident and too calculated this time around for Fabio to pose much of a threat, and he'll get taken out again. I think Daniel will pick up where he left off, making it an easier and quicker win than the first fight. But let's see!"

Darren Barker - former middleweight world champion

"The first fight was called 'don't blink' and I think it should be a legal requirement that you do not blink for this rematch either. It has every single component required to be an absolute barnstormer.

"Wardley was second best last time. He had his moments but he is going to have to up his game. Dubois' confidence now will take him into another stratosphere and makes him a very tough man to beat. I feel his jab and his know-how, and the new-found self belief, will be the difference.

"But - and this is a big but - I'm not completely ruling out Wardley."

Michael 'Venom' Page - former UFC fighter

"It's interesting because Fabio Wardley landed a big shot very early in the first fight and I think weirdly enough that earlier success messed him up. What he ended up doing was button bashing the same shot he landed right at the beginning and Dubois kept anticipating it after that. Wardley didn't adjust and I'm surprised he didn't.

"If he's able to be smarter, land those kind of shots but also find a few other angles, that's a dangerous fight Wardley can win. But Dubois is a beast and will learn really well, I was impressed in that fight he learned while being hurt which is difficult. He's an aggressive person, a big power puncher. Some small adjustments and Wardley can turn it around but I will have to put my money on Dubois."

"My prediction for this is a little bit biased because we are in the same gym so I'm Team Wardley no matter what, even though I've known Dubois since he was 15.

"I do believe Wardley has the capability to get the win this time. It should be a great fight and I hope both men put on a great display for everyone to see and go home happy to their families."

Paul Smith - former world title challenger

"I fancy Dubois between the middle to late rounds. I think Wardley will come out fast and put it on him and that's his best chance. I wouldn't be surprised if he won early, but I think Dubois has his number.

"Wardley took a lot in that fight and that took a lot out of him. I don't see him trying to box Dubois, the only chance he has is to jump him on early. I think Dubois will match him and weather the storm and use his feet like he did last time to nullify whatever Wardley does."

"I've never gotten a Dubois pick wrong. I am on record as saying he would be a world champion long before he achieved it, yet had him losing to Joe Joyce and twice against Oleksandr Usyk. However, I did predict he'd stop both Anthony Joshua and Fabio Wardley back in May.

"He's a much better mover and more agile than he's given credit for and now has a level of experience you can't manufacture, as we saw when he wisely took a knee in the first fight.

"In a battle between a puncher and a boxer (who can also punch), always go with the more accomplished fighter. Dubois by TKO, likely a little earlier than last time - as Wardley's corner won't be so brave second time around."

"It's the rematch of 2026 after one of the greatest heavyweight fights we've seen on our shores. The first encounter had everything – thrills and spills, blood, brutality and boxing at its very best.

"Will it be repeat or revenge? Dubois is the world champion and favourite going in, but can Wardley find the power to keep Dubois down this time? Or does Dubois' confidence and power carry him through?

"Both are predicting wins within five rounds. I see this as a knockout, but I'm not sure which way."

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"I'm going to be the difference. I am going to back Fabio Wardley by knockout within six rounds. Yep, I said. I'm going for Fab within six."

articles.title: ‘Let’s see who the best is’: Frank Warren opens the door to Oleksandr Usyk’s heavyweight title return
articles.summary: Unbeaten heavyweight great Oleksandr Usyk was the undisputed champion but vacated all his belts; He is though expected to return next year for a final fight and if he wants to reclaim a world title, promoter Frank Warren urges him to "come and see us" for a top-level fight
articles.body:
The unbeaten Ukrainian was the undisputed heavyweight champion but vacated all his belts and isn't expected to box again until next year.

But if he is planning a 'last dance' bout, promoter Frank Warren could provide a top-level opponent.

Warren promotes WBC champion Agit Kabayel, WBO heavyweight titlist Daniel Dubois and also represents Tyson Fury, who stands to win the WBA 'super' belt if can beat Anthony Joshua in December.

Usyk has beaten Fury and Dubois before, though a trilogy bout with either could still become a major fight.

Taking on Kabayel for the WBC crown at a stadium in Germany could also be appealing.

"I'll take that fight [for Kabayel], I wouldn't mind that fight," Warren told Sky Sports .

"Any of them," the promoter continued. "There are some great fights to be made and we'll make them.

"He can do what he likes," Warren said of Usyk, "but if he wants to fight one of these guys, then come and see us. It's not hard for us to do. We've worked together on quite a few occasions now, we got on very well and we've delivered.

"He'll want to be at the top so he'll want to fight the best ones so let's see who it is."

Dubois came unstuck on the previous occasions he fought Usyk. But he came roaring back to defeat Fabio Wardley in a thriller to win the WBO heavyweight title. If he can score a repeat victory over Wardley in their rematch at The O2 Arena in London, Dubois will look to take over next year as the best heavyweight in the world.

"That's the aim, that's our objective," Dubois' trainer Don Charles told Sky Sports . "It would be foolish of me to overlook Saturday.

"Fabio's a serious, serious fighter. A very determined fighter. He's ambitious, quite rightly so and he's a former world champion.

"He's going to do everything in his physical make up and desire to try and recapture his title and it's down to us say no you can't have it, we're having it for keeps."

articles.title: DIY SOS to be 'rested' next year to save money, BBC says
articles.summary: The long-running programme will be replaced by a "more cost-effective" spin-off show revisiting past projects.
articles.body:
The long-running home renovation TV series DIY SOS will be "rested" next year in the light of "savings challenges", the BBC has said.

It will be replaced by a spin-off show featuring highlights from past episodes. Sources denied reports in the Sun newspaper the programme would be axed as part of a plan to make savings.

Presented by Nick Knowles, DIY SOS sees a team transform the homes of families who are facing severe illness, disability, bereavement or building disasters.

It was first broadcast in 1999 and is currently airing its 35th series on BBC One and iPlayer.

The decision comes during the corporation's drive to save £500m over three years. It has already cancelled several well-known TV shows including Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live At The Apollo.

A BBC spokesperson said: "In light of the BBC's savings challenges we have taken the decision to rest DIY SOS in 2027 and commission a new spin-off show instead from producers South Shore.

"DIY SOS Rebuilt My Life will revisit successes from the show's past and expand the brand on the BBC in a more cost-effective way next year."

After initially concentrating on small-scale renovations, DIY SOS shifted focus to tackle a number of more ambitious projects throughout its multiple-decade run.

Among them was a 2015 special that saw hundreds of volunteers work alongside Knowles, Prince William and Prince Harry to build housing for veterans in Manchester.

William returned to the programme in 2018 for a two-part special supporting survivors and the community affected by the Grenfell Tower fire.

The emotional episodes saw the team build a new community centre and restore the Dale Youth Boxing Club, which was destroyed in the disaster.

The programme's latest episode saw the team overhaul a family's property to allow their 17-year-old son Dan - who has complex disabilities - to receive treatment at home after spending more than three years in hospital.

Dan's father, Nigel, told the BBC it was a "miracle".

articles.title: Henry Cejudo reveals Jon Jones visited him six times after praising his fight breakdowns
articles.summary: Henry Cejudo has revealed how Jon Jones personally reached out to him after watching his detailed fight breakdowns.
articles.body: Henry Cejudo has revealed how Jon Jones personally reached out to him after watching his detailed fight breakdowns. The former two-division UFC champion said Jones was so impressed by his analysis that he told Cejudo, “I couldn’t explain myself better than what you did.”Cejudo said Jones later visited him on six separate occasions to learn and work with him. However, Cejudo stressed that he never viewed himself as Jones’ coach. Instead, he compared the heavyweight great to a Lamborghini that only needed to be polished before another major challenge.Henry Cejudo explains how he helped Jon Jones sharpen his skillsHenry Cejudo’s relationship with Jon Jones grew from his detailed analysis of MMA fights. The Olympic gold medallist became known for breaking down fighters and explaining the technical aspects of their games on his YouTube channel.Jones, who was preparing for his move to heavyweight at the time, apparently paid close attention to Cejudo’s work. The former UFC light heavyweight champion eventually contacted Cejudo himself after watching one of his breakdowns.According to Cejudo, Jones praised his ability to explain the fighter’s game and gave him a major compliment, “I couldn’t explain myself better than what you did.”That conversation eventually led to Jones visiting Cejudo multiple times.Cejudo has revealed that Jones came to work with him on six different occasions. Their sessions were particularly relevant ahead of Jones’ heavyweight debut against Ciryl Gane at UFC 285 in March 2023.Jones travelled to Phoenix, Arizona, where he worked with Cejudo and coach Eric Albarracin at Fight Ready. The sessions focused on sharpening Jones’ skills and helping him prepare for the challenges of competing at heavyweight.However, Cejudo has always been careful about describing his role in Jones’ development.He did not believe that Jones needed someone to teach him how to fight. Jones had already established himself as one of the greatest fighters in MMA history.Instead, Cejudo viewed his contribution as helping an already elite fighter make small improvements. That is where his famous Lamborghini comparison comes in.For Cejudo, Jones was already a high-end machine. He simply wanted to help polish it and make sure everything was working at the highest possible level.The collaboration also highlighted the respect between two of the most accomplished fighters in combat sports.Cejudo won Olympic gold in wrestling at the 2008 Beijing Games before becoming a UFC champion in two weight classes. Jones, meanwhile, built a legendary career at light heavyweight before moving up to heavyweight and winning the vacant UFC heavyweight title.Cejudo’s own wrestling background made his experience particularly valuable to Jones. articles.title: UFC ring girl goes from octagons to painting Tom Brady artwork for Fanatics, woke concerts & college football
articles.summary: Brittney Palmer pivoted from a 16-year UFC ring girl career to creating baseball cards for Topps and painting NFL jerseys for Fanatics.
articles.body: Welcome to Screencaps, "America's Best Daily Column," as named by the readers. Screencaps, which publishes seven-days-a-week, is a mix of sports, pop culture, and emails from sane readers from around the world. This column isn't for the coastal elites. Give us a week to steal your heart. Our track record is pretty good. Let's have some fun. What happens to UFC Ring Girls after they hang up their ring girl attire? I have to give Brittney Palmer credit. After a 16-year career walking around UFC octagons for so many Saturday nights, there comes a point where a ring girl knows she has lost a step and needs to pivot. Then comes retirement. For many of these women, there's no senior circuit for ring girls. There's no Senior PGA Tour. Some turn to OnlyFans to keep the lights on. The easy way out. It's true, Palmer has any OnlyFans account, but she's also one of the hottest sports artists in the United States right now. She's making art on OF and designing baseball cards for Topps and is now even creating artwork on NFL jerseys for a Fanatics project called Under Wraps where fans pay $500 or more to buy a mystery jersey box. Someone will walk away with this piece of art - from a UFC legend. Mailbag Saturday...where I dump out the emails before heading over to the soccer fields to watch Screencaps the III's team get destroyed • Adam in Nebraska checks in: Give me 80s/90s college football. Give me 80s/90s Wendy’s Years from now I’m gonna be more fired up for Maction, and MTN west than any SEC/ BTN Saturday in October. We cannot lose what football meant to this country. COLLEGE FOOTBALL RATINGS ARE DOWN DOUBLE DIGITS SO FAR THIS SEASON • Galen in Sunset Beach, NC is ready for the third Saturday in October: A sacred day in the South today…The Third Saturday In October! The historic day that pits the Tennessee Volunteers vs the Alabama Crimson Tide. Ironically, it was 56 years ago on this very date! I was with my Dad and we won 24-0. That was the last time the two teams wore their home jerseys for the game. 56 years later, they are doing it again today. Should be quite a spectacle! Go Vols! • Lee D. in Tampa is frustrated over the 24-team playoff: Well, the suits killed the golden goose. Nothing like watching Tulane vs. Iowa. This guy won't be watching that. Just like I have yet to watch a play-in game (no offense to Dayton) in the NCAA tournament (64 teams was the sweet spot), I have no interest in watching Liberty vs. Ole Miss or SMU vs. Indiana. They can have their playoff games. Doesn't mean I have to watch. When the playoffs get down to the quarterfinals, then I'll start paying attention. This is what happens when a major conference hires a network suit with a baseball background to run things. Go google "Tony Petitti" and watch what pops up. It's not Tony Petitti, Big Ten commissioner, it's "Tony Petitti, television producer." Think it was back in the summer at B1G football media days that he was visibly astonished why fans wouldn't want more playoff games and he openly touted how college football should be like baseball and basically double the number of playoff games. Dude, did you even watch last year's first round games? No one who saw those box scores would demand more of the same, or worse. The BCS had the number of playoff games right (eight). They just weren't smart enough to use that format as a quarterfinal round. What would have been better is if the B1G and SEC decided to have a four-team playoff for the conference title. Those are games that fans would want to watch and all the TV suits would be happy with the eyeballs. Yeah, trade the conference title games for James Madison vs. Oregon (and more FCS vs. B1G/SEC games to open the season). What a friggin' trainwreck! ... as for Elon Musk's new flying car, this makes Kirby Smart very nervous. • Brad S. on woke concerts: Back in 1979, the 'cause célèbre' of the week was No Nukes. (I think it fell between the Acid Rain and Ozone Hole movements.) Of course, they had a big concert in Central Park to 'raise awareness' (read: sell albums). Anyway, Jackson Browne was a part of that concert and toured soon after that. One of his stops was the Assembly Hall at the University of Illinois. It became apparent that neither the singer nor his staff did any research as to the where he was playing, because they would have discovered the U of I has a huge Engineering College and one of the top Nuclear Engineering programs in the world. Well, about four songs in, Jackson Browne decides to start his spiel about 'No Nukes' and how there was a nuke plant near Champaign, and everyone should 'duck and cover' or some crap like that. (The Clinton Nuclear plant is about 40 miles west of the campus.) GOO GOO DOLLS' JOHN RZEZNIK DRAWS LINE ON POLITICS AT CONCERTS: 'I'M NOT GOING TO LECTURE YOU' After about three minutes, someone from the crowd yelled, "Shut up and sing!" and it got a huge round of applause. Jackson Browne looked visibly pissed off! He played the rest of the show, but did not utter another word! This should be the proper way to handle things, whenever these idiot artists decide to rant. Random things that I've been wondering about: Do people still throw all the coats on a bed when there's a gathering at a house? Mrs. Screencaps lit up this morning over this question. I'm talking a deep dive into the memories of her life. Here at our house, we typically pile up the coats on a living room chair that is sacrificed instead of people trudging upstairs to drop a coat. But there's something about that memory deep in all of our brains of going into your grandmother's bedroom to get the coats before leaving. According to Gemini, the coat thing dates back to the 19th century when there were dedicated spaces in houses for guests to "de-layer," as the historians call it. The coat thing would evolve. Etiquette writers told women in the 1920s to instruct female guests to de-layer in dressing rooms, typically on the second level. Men were not expected to de-layer upstairs. Eventually, the WWII veterans bought one-story houses in the suburbs and the de-layering tradition was modified to what many of us still do today. There you go. When people de-layer in your bedroom before card night, they're keeping a 19th century tradition alive. • Homebrew Bill in Nebraska checks in on the topic of having people over in 2026: Wanted to chime in on this topic. I'm guessing there are others in the group in the same boat. We live in a decent neighborhood and have really good friends right next door and are friendly with a half-dozen other neighbors. We hardly ever host anymore or go anywhere primarily because my wife is a bit OCD and is very introverted. Keep in mind, it's not that our house is unkempt. Our best friends next door know that and they've seen our home "lived in". But if we do invite them over my wife thinks everything needs to be done like we're listing the house for a realtor. On the rare occasions I have friend(s) over for a beer I get grief because there might be dog hair in the basement. Most of the time those meetings occur in the garage where the keg fridge is. It's frustrating at times. • Mark from NC seems to hate people: I think the TV show "Friends" was the worst TV in history….and I’ve never watched one episode. If you’re that age, and you’re hanging out in someone else’s living room, you’ve yet to assume adult responsibilities…..like being married, having kids, having a job. I haven’t hung out at someone else house since maybe a few times in my 20’s and that was over 40 years ago. If someone even thinks about coming to my house, I’ll be sure to hear from my wife "Don’t let them in the house." • Phil in Florida likes to pack his house: I personally love having people over. I don’t have to drive, the party ends when I want it to, and I usually am left with fuller beer fridge than before I started. Also fun things happen, like when I had 1 friend come over, then her roommate, then roommate’s friends, and before you know it my girlfriend came home to a house full of people that she didn’t know, all having a great time. I was in so much trouble after everyone left. My mom’s side of the family is excellent at these type of shenanigans as well. I will forever carry with me the morning I found myself smoking a cigarette in my parent’s lanai putting together the pieces of the night before, when my sister walked outside and I asked her "Did grandma die yesterday and then we threw a huge rager?" She said "Yes, that is exactly what happened." If there is a room containing a bed for you, and has a door, hell yeah, have people over. You can’t tell stories about not having people over. I will refrain from discussing the Bears or anything Chicago. We don’t wanna talk right now. Have a good one CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE A Dodgers fan deals with the World Series domination coming to an end • Scott in Rocky Point, NY puts it all in perspective: Officially, I'm a 51 yr old Dodgers fan. Family was hauled to Lake Havasu, AZ in 1975 and the only baseball we watched was Dodger baseball (out of a Vegas TV channel). So, became a Dodgers fan. So many highs, so many lows. Garvey, Cey, Lopes, Russell infield. Fernando Valenzuela. Almost busting my hand on the ceiling watching Kirk Gibson's HR off Eckersley. Mr. October beating Dodgers. Dodgers beating Yankees in '24. Machado failure. Piazza. Etc. Etc. Etc. But, even though a huge Dodgers fan, I'm an equal baseball fan. Played it and dreamt of a future in it. Don't hate teams (except for those evil Braves). My take on this year's Dodgers' exit - sucks but well deserved series sweep by the Brewers. A team that played as a team and won as a team. Had that "feeling" early on game one that it just wasn't happening for my Dodgers. And when an entire team are playing poorly, the writing was on the wall. And seeing how the Brewers were playing, that's what makes baseball, baseball. Fun to see a team that hasn't been to the series in 44 years. I don't care about large market teams vs small market teams, that's for the bean counters and "never played the game" dorks. While MLB and the networks airing the WS want large market teams ($$$), this World Series (guessing Brewers v Guardians) will be fun to watch. I'm going with Brewers taking it all and last game being in Milwaukee to give their fans what they've been missing. 📩 Email: joe.kinsey@outkick.comSend photos, stories, tips, rants—whatever you've got. articles.title: Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj: ¿Dónde ver la pelea y a qué hora empieza hoy en México?

articles.summary: Fundora se enfrenta a Hadribeaj se enfrentan por el título superwelter del CMB. Conoce horario, transmisión, cartelera, momios y pronóstico
articles.body: El boxeo internacional tiene una cita importante este sábado 17 de octubre con Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj, combate en el que estará en juego el campeonato mundial superwelter del CMB. El estadounidense vuelve al ring después de vencer por nocaut técnico a Keith Thurman en marzo. Del otro lado estará un retador que llega invicto y con la oportunidad más importante de su carrera. Hadribeaj buscará dar la sorpresa en Las Vegas, aunque tendrá enfrente a un campeón que cuenta con una considerable ventaja de estatura y experiencia, pero la bolsa de la pelea de Fundora vs Hadribeaj es bastante considerable. La función se realizará este sábado 17 de octubre de 2026 en The Chelsea, dentro de The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Para México, la transmisión de la cartelera principal está programada a partir de las 18:00 horas, tiempo del centro, mientras que el combate estelar está previsto alrededor de las 21:00 horas, dependiendo de la duración de las peleas anteriores. Los aficionados en México podrán seguir Fundora vs Hadribeaj en vivo por DAZN, plataforma que transmitirá la función mediante streaming. Asimismo, por MARCA MX podrás seguir el minuto a minuto del enfrentamiento. El combate de Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj pondrá en juego el cinturón superwelter del CMB, en una pelea pactada a 12 asaltos. La función organizada por Premier Boxing Champions tendrá otros enfrentamientos destacados: Fundora parte como amplio favorito. Sus 1.97 metros de estatura y aproximadamente 2.03 metros de alcance representan una diferencia física considerable ante Hadribeaj, quien mide cerca de 1.78 metros. El pronóstico apunta a una victoria de Fundora por nocaut técnico en los rounds intermedios o finales. Sin embargo, Hadribeaj llega invicto y podría complicar al campeón si consigue cerrar distancias y obligarlo a pelear en corto. Las líneas varían dependiendo de la casa de apuestas. Una de las referencias disponibles coloca a Fundora alrededor de -1250, mientras que Hadribeaj aparece en +700 y el empate en +900. Estos momios reflejan la condición de amplio favorito del campeón, aunque pueden cambiar antes del inicio. La diferencia física y la experiencia de Sebastian Fundora lo colocan en una posición privilegiada, pero una victoria de Hadribeaj cambiaría por completo el panorama de las 154 libras. Para el campeón, retener el cinturón podría acercarlo a una futura pelea de unificación, con Jaron “Boots” Ennis entre los nombres que aparecen en el horizonte.

articles.standfirst: Se impuso por decisión mayoritaria a Nabiev, que estaba invicto
articles.summary: Se impuso por decisión mayoritaria a Nabiev, que estaba invicto
articles.body: Lo prometió... y lo hizo. David Mora (11-7) se estrenó en Rkena con victoria. El madrileño del Black Panther Gym venció por decisión mayoritaria (29-27x2, 28-28) al azerí Alim Nabiev (4-1), al que arrebató el invicto. Es el primer triunfo de Mora en tres años y la vuelta a la senda del triunfo para el que en su día fue campeón de AFL. Sin duda, una de las mayores victorias de la carrera del español. O incluso, la más grande. Nabiev, con poca experiencia en MMA, es una leyenda de K1 y kickboxing habiendo logrado numerosos títulos en más de 70 peleas en dichas disciplinas. Pero esto son artes marciales mixtas... y la polivalencia de Mora en ese campo le valió para vencer. También los errores de su rival. El árbitro quitó un punto a Nabiev (representando a Azerbaiyán pero de familia georgiana, y muy apoyado en Tiflis) por agarrarse de la jaula para huir de un momento de control del español. Mora era muy superior en el suelo y pese a sufrir dos 'knockdowns' en contra... supo sobrevivir. Se llevó el combate a aguas profundas y pese a que no fue el triunfo más espectacular de una velada repleta de finalizaciones... es una victoria. Y muy necesaria para un David Mora que a sus 31 años remonta el vuelo ganando en la promotora que lidera la siempre competitiva escena georgiana en la actualidad.

articles.title: AEW Star 'Pac' Benjamin Satterley's Cause of Death Confirmed by Medical Examiner
articles.summary: The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office determined this week that former AEW and WWE star Pac died last month as a result of bronchial asthma.
articles.body:
The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office determined this week that former AEW and WWE star Pac died last month as a result of bronchial asthma.

A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office in Chicago shared the findings Friday with Edward Lewis of the California Post .

Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, was found unconscious in a rental car in the parking lot of a Des Plaines, Illinois, restaurant on Sept. 27, and he was later pronounced dead.

The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office ruled that Pac's death was natural.

One day earlier, Pac wrestled on AEW's All Out card, which took place at Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois.

In the opening match of the show, Pac challenged Andrade El Idolo for the National Championship. Andrade prevailed in what was a highly regarded bout.

Originally from Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Pac was part of AEW since its inception in 2019, and he went on to hold the All-Atlantic Championship once and World Trios Championships twice.

Prior to joining AEW, Pac wrestled under the names Neville and Adrian Neville in WWE from 2012 to 2018.

As part of the NXT roster, Pac was a one-time NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion, and he later held the WWE Cruiserweight Championship twice.

articles.title: Raoni Barcelos breaks silence on UFC collapse, reveals frightening symptoms and possible retirement
articles.summary: Raoni Barcelos is still waiting to learn why he lost consciousness during his UFC Vegas 121 main event against Raul Rosas Jr. on September 26.
articles.body: Raoni Barcelos is still waiting to learn why he lost consciousness during his UFC Vegas 121 main event against Raul Rosas Jr. on September 26. The 39-year-old Brazilian says his whole body went numb before he blacked out. Nearly three weeks later, he feels better each day, but doctors have yet to give him a clear answer. Speaking to MMA Fighting, Barcelos confirmed that he is undergoing more medical tests in Las Vegas. He hopes to fight again, although he admits retirement remains a possibility.Raoni Barcelos Awaits Medical Results After Losing Consciousness Against Raul Rosas Jr.Barcelos said the frightening episode began with a sudden loss of feeling throughout his body. He remembers nothing about what happened next until he woke up in an ambulance and asked his father to explain the situation.“Unfortunately, we don’t know what happened,” Barcelos told MMA Fighting. “It was a sudden illness. I fell ill, and I felt my whole body really starting to go numb. After that, I don’t remember anything. I only remember coming to in the ambulance, asking my father what had happened, and him trying to explain it to me as best he could.”The incident happened during the fifth round of his fight with Rosas Jr. Barcelos was ahead on the judges’ scorecards when he suddenly lost consciousness. The referee stopped the contest, giving Rosas Jr. a technical knockout win. Barcelos was taken to a Level 1 trauma center for medical care.The UFC confirmed on September 27 that Barcelos was stable, alert and responsive after a CT scan and a medical assessment. However, his latest update shows that the cause of the collapse remains unclear.“I’m undergoing a battery of tests here in Vegas. I had another MRI on Monday and we’re waiting for a good result,” he said. “The doctor hasn’t released the results yet, and everything is being kept very confidential, but I feel better every day.”Former UFC champion Glover Teixeira, who was in Barcelos’ corner, said earlier in October that doctors had found some swelling in the fighter’s brain. However, Barcelos is still waiting for doctors to explain exactly what caused him to collapse.Raoni Barcelos Has Not Ruled Out Retirement After His Health ScareDespite the uncertainty, Barcelos has not given up on his fighting career. He is visiting the UFC Performance Institute in Las Vegas for physical therapy and neurological tests while doctors continue to assess his condition.Still, the Brazilian understands that his health must come first. He admitted that retirement could happen, even though he does not want to think about leaving the sport right now.“It hasn’t been ruled out. This is a very difficult time because we’re athletes, we’re fighters, and you never want to stop,” Barcelos said. “A lot of the time, your body can’t take it anymore, but your mind keeps you going. We really need to give it time to see what the future holds. But I want to make it clear right now that I don’t want to stop.”Barcelos has also spoken with his father, Davi Ramos, Andre Felipe and Teixeira about what comes next. He said they advised him to focus on recovery instead of making a decision while the incident is still fresh.“A lot of people have already retired me before my time laughs, but I really need this time to figure out what comes next,” he added.For now, Barcelos has been told to avoid head strikes for six months and keep his heart rate within a safe range. He must complete his medical checks before considering a return to full training.The Brazilian still wants to compete, but his next step depends on what doctors discover. articles.title: Daniel Dubois smashes through Fabio Wardley to win WBO heavyweight world championship rematch in the second round
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois defeated Fabio Wardley with savage speed and focused aggression to defend the WBO heavyweight world title at the O2 Arena in London; Dubois ended the fight in the second round; the British rivals were rematching after Dubois won an epic brawl in their first fight in May
articles.body:
Dubois retained the WBO heavyweight title he won from Wardley in May in crushing style, picking up just where he left off in their first fight.

Dubois and Wardley were renewing hostilities only five months after a frenetic and ultimately brutal contest.

Then London's Dubois had needed to rise twice from early knockdowns to punch out a savage 11-round victory over Wardley, hurting the Ipswich fighter even though Wardley was stopped on his feet.

Wardley, determined to win back his world title as soon as he could, exercised the rematch clause in his contract and forced this second fight to take place.

But Dubois snuffed out his hopes with brutal speed.

A smashing Dubois right cross saw Wardley drop, ever so briefly, to a knee in the opening seconds of the first round. He bounced up immediately, inviting the right uppercut that followed.

The referee administered a count, and that proved to be just a momentary reprieve. Dubois set about him with shuddering force for the rest of the round.

Wardley was pained, being driven to the ropes by an unrelenting Dubois.

The champion continued his onslaught in the second round. He hammered Wardey into a corner, jolting his head on his neck with a salvo of stunning punches, until Wardley's trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel and the referee rushed in to end it.

On the undercard Bakhodir Jalolov , a two-time Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist, showcased just what makes him so formidable as he hammered out a 10 round unanimous decision victory over Solomon Dacres.

But he also displayed what can make him so frustrating to watch. The towering southpaw controlled virtually the whole bout and struck Dacres over early in the fifth round.

The knockdown was superb, Jalolov using his right to take Dacres' left glove away from his guard, opening up a path for the Uzbek's booming left cross - a shot that sent Dacres to the canvas and bloodied his nose.

But Jalolov didn't capitalise and continued to work in single shots, albeit excellent single shots, as he dominated without turning up the pressure, winning 99-91 and 99-90 twice.

20-year-old Irish heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan made short work of journeyman Dan Garber.

In his fifth pro fight, Olaniyan maintained his 100 percent finish rate stopping Garber in the second round.

Busy without rushing his work, Olaniyan's right cranked Garber's back into a corner post at the end of the first round.

He picked up from there for the second, trapping Garber on the ropes and putting him down with another heavy cross.

Garber's corner threw in the towel, then threw in a second. But the referee kicked them out the ring and Garber tried to fight on. He was though promptly crumpled a second time. After rising unsteadily the referee waved it off at 1-15.

articles.title: Dubois vs Wardley 2: Londoner retains title with dominant second-round stoppage
articles.summary: WBO world champion Daniel Dubois underlines his status as Britain's leading heavyweight with a devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley.
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois underlined his status as Britain's leading heavyweight with a devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain his WBO title in London.

The 29-year-old floored Wardley with a straight right inside the opening 20 seconds of their eagerly anticipated rematch at the O2 Arena and continued his relentless assault.

Wardley survived the opening round but was overwhelmed by another sustained attack in the second, prompting his corner to throw in the towel.

Dubois registers a second successive stoppage victory over Wardley, just five months after climbing off the canvas twice to dethrone his British rival in a thrilling 11-round contest in Manchester.

This time, there was no such drama for the champion, who was dominant from the opening bell as he extended his professional record to 24 wins - 23 by knockout - and three defeats.

"Fabio is a great boy, coming in for the second time, but it was my time and my era. I had my intentions, bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said.

"My back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did tonight."

Wardley, 31, suffered the second defeat of his 23-fight professional career.

"I have always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, the best in the business, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around so, there is no shame in a loss when you're testing yourself against the best," he said.

Dubois comes out with intent in one-sided title defence

A sell-out crowd of 19,000 packed the O2 Arena and made their allegiances clear.

Wardley's charismatic yet measured personality has made him a popular figure. He looked full of purpose as he took his time on stage, fireworks exploding in front of him, his usual smile replaced by a look of determination.

Dubois, meanwhile, was greeted by jeers as he marched straight past the fireworks and towards the ring, wasting little time soaking up the occasion.

Actor Paddy Considine, comedian Rob Beckett, Oasis star Noel Gallagher and darts world champion Luke Littler were among the famous faces in attendance.

With 41 knockouts between the fighters, few expected the judges to be called upon. The feeling beforehand was that Wardley's best chance lay in making another fast start, having dropped Dubois inside the opening moments of their first meeting.

But in a stunning reversal, it took just 17 seconds for Wardley to hit the canvas as Dubois backed him into a corner and landed a straight right.

Chants of 'oh Fabio Wardley' were quickly silenced as Dubois continued to unload punishing combinations. Another furious attack towards the end of the round left Wardley in deep trouble.

Trainer Ben Davison, criticised for not withdrawing Wardley sooner in their first contest, stood poised with a towel in his hand as his fighter survived to the bell.

There had already been concerns over whether Wardley had returned too quickly after the punishment he absorbed in May, when he was left bloodied and badly swollen.

And those fears appeared justified as the challenger struggled to cope with Dubois' relentless pressure. Wardley's hands were low and his punches wild and telegraphed, lacking the menace he had shown in Manchester.

Backed into the corner again in the second round, he was subjected to another barrage before Davison leapt up and threw in the towel.

The two men could hardly be more different outside the ring. Dubois was typically reserved throughout fight week, looking uncomfortable in the media spotlight. Wardley, by contrast, was relaxed and articulate, insisting he had learned from his mistakes.

But despite their contrasting personalities and fierce rivalry, there was mutual respect at the end of the fight.

Lucrative nights await for Dubois & Wardley's losing gamble

Dubois continues to fly the flag for British heavyweight boxing. After losing to Oleksandr Usyk in 2023, he responded with impressive victories over Jarrell Miller, Filip Hrgovic and Anthony Joshua, only to suffer another defeat by Usyk last year.

But back-to-back stoppage victories over Wardley have reinforced his standing among the world's leading active heavyweights.

IBF champion Hrgovic, whom Dubois stopped in June 2024, entered the ring afterwards, with both men keen on a rematch.

However, promoter Frank Warren wants Hrgovic to make his first title defence in Croatia before pursuing a unification fight.

The biggest payday for Dubois could come against the winner of Joshua and Tyson Fury's December showdown, which is expected to have the WBA 'super' title at stake.

Asked who he wants to face next, Dubois said: "Whoever is next in line, really. I'm the champion now, and I want to get some big fights in. At this stage in my career, big money, big fights."

For Wardley, successive defeats represent a significant setback, but his remarkable journey should not be forgotten.

The former recruitment consultant had just four white-collar fights before turning professional in 2017. Less than a decade later, he was a world heavyweight champion.

Rather than rebuild against lesser opposition following May's punishing defeat, Wardley gambled on an immediate rematch with one of the division's most destructive punchers.

It was a gamble that backfired and, after two bruising defeats, he may benefit from some time away.
