articles.title: Joaquin Buckley gives bizarre, completely silent interview at UFC Edmonton
articles.summary: Joaquin Buckley has never shied away from the spotlight during fight week. But ahead of his main event bout against Mike Malott at UFC Edmonton on Saturday,...
articles.body:
Joaquin Buckley has never shied away from the spotlight during fight week. But ahead of his main event bout against Mike Malott at UFC Edmonton on Saturday, the typically outspoken welterweight took a very different approach.

During Friday's ceremonial weigh-ins, Buckley refused to shake Dana White's hand when the UFC CEO extended it on stage. Instead, Buckley ignored White and went straight into his face-off with Malott, never breaking eye contact with his opponent.

Shortly after the weigh-ins, Buckley was pulled aside for an interview with UFC on Paramount+, but he didn't answer a single question. Instead, Buckley simply stared straight into the camera for the entire minute-long interview as Mackenzie Pavlovich tried to ask him about his preparation and mindset.

The new persona is quite the change for Buckley, who has built a reputation as one of the more vocal and playful fighters on the UFC roster. But there's probably a reason why he's ramping up the intensity a bit.

Buckley enters Saturday's fight on a two-fight losing streak, and he admitted that he expected that he would be cut from the UFC with a loss in his previous fight at UFC 328. That obviously didn't happen, as Buckley is back for another fight, but it seems like he's taking quite a different approach this time around.

Malott, meanwhile, is riding a four-fight win streak and will be fighting in front of a home crowd in Canada.

articles.summary: El estadounidense perdió la batalla ante la báscula y pierde su oportunidad de defender el título
articles.body: El boxeador estadounidense, Brandon Figueroa, se ha convertido en el primer perdedor de la cartelera sabatina tras no cumplir el peso reglamentario de 126 libras en la Ceremonia de Pesaje por un exceso de 1.4 libras. Tuvo una segunda oportunidad al mediodía de este sábado en el lugar del evento, pero el campeón pluma de la AMB no intentó volver a pesarse en la báscula y fue oficialmente despojado de su título. Ante esta situación, el Comité Organizador, con validez de la AMB, decidieron cancelar la pelea de Campeonato Mundial del peso pluma y Figueroa ha sido despojado de su título tras no dar el peso esta semana. Lo que pudo haber sido una noche gloriosa para el pugilista de raíces mexicanas se convirtió en un rotundo fracaso una vez que la noche sabatina sería su primera defensa como campeón de las 126 libras y su combate estaba programado contra Tomoki Kameda. Tras el retiro de Brandon Figueroa, donde presumiblemente tuvo problemas de salud para dar con el peso, el título pluma de la Asociación Mundial de Boxeo (AMB) quedó vacante. Aunque inicialmente se negoció continuar con la pelea contra Tomoki Kameda bajo una compensación económica (donde solo Kameda podía ganar el cinturón), la pelea fue oficialmente cancelada. Con el despojo de la faja en poder de Brandon Figueroa, el cetro mundial de las 126 libras de la AMB queda oficialmente vacante a la espera de que el organismo determine a los próximos contendientes para disputarlo. El combate sería el combate coestelar de la cartelera Sebastián Fundora y Ermal Hadribeaj en el Salón de Espectáculos "The Chelsea" del complejo "The Cosmopolitan" en Las Vegas, Nevada. Oficialmente, Figueroa se retiró el sábado por la mañana para no exponer su integridad física al tener que bajar casi 3 kilos, lo cual llegaría muy debilitado ante la furia del japonés. Brandon Figueroa ganó el título de la AMB con un nocaut en el duodécimo asalto sobre Nick Ball en febrero de 2026 en Liverpool, y esta noche se había programado su primera defensa del peso pluma. De este modo, la cartelera entre Fundora vs Hadribeaj se ha modificado y la pelea previa entre Armando Reséndiz (16-3, 11 KOs) y Koen Maxoudier (16-4, 6 KOs), combate a 10 asaltos en la categoría de peso supermediano, ha sido ascendido al nuevo evento coestelar. articles.title: AEW WrestleDream 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW WrestleDream 2026.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW WrestleDream 2026.

Here's a look at the card AEW advertised for the show:

Mercedes Mone vs. Thekla (Women's World Championship)

The Young Bucks vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight (AEW Tag Team Championships)

Jon Moxley vs. Mark Davis (Continental Championship)

Swerve Strickland and New Level vs. Adam Page and Brodido (Trios Championships)

Andrade El Idolo vs. Tommaso Ciampa (National Championship)

Persephone vs. Hyan vs. Dani Luna vs. Queen Aminata (TBS Championship)

Will Ospreay vs. Samoa Joe vs. Mike Bailey vs. Adam Copeland vs. Kazuchika Okada vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Darby Allin vs. Ricochet (World Heavyweight Championship)

Let's take a look at everything that happened at this year's WrestleDream.

The first match on the one-hour pre-show saw Julia Hart and Skye Blue take on Megan Bayne and Lena Kross. Despite the former tag champs having a big size and power advantage, Blue and Skye used their quickness and speed to keep the action competitive.

Heel vs. heel matches usually aren't ideal, but these four women all have enough fans that the crowd felt invested. Bayne and Kross felt like they had a slight edge, though.

This was a high-energy bout with some fun moments. The fact that it was more back-and-forth than most of Divine Dominion's matches definitely made The Sisters of Sin look strong. Despite a good effort, Kross and Bayne were still too much for them and ended up getting the win.

Result: Divine Dominion defeated Sisters of Sin

Jake Doyle, Josh Alexander and Wardlow vs. Three Jobbers

The Don Callis Family was given an easy match when Jake Doyle, Wardlow and Josh Alexander beat the life out of three local talents. There was nothing competitive about this. They may as well have been throwing three training dummies around because the jobbers did not get in a single shred of offense.

This was so one-sided that it can't even be graded properly. It was fun to watch the crowd get behind Wardlow hitting multiple powerbombs again, but that was about all this had to offer. At least the fans seemed to be having fun with it.

Result: Wardlow, Alexander and Doyle won

Does anyone else miss Julia Hart's old entrance? It was one of the best in AEW.

Kross had the "I've been misted" eye makeup.

Bayne and Kross have somehow been even more impressive since losing the titles.

It's going to be interesting to see how Wardlow is used and whether he and MJF ever reignite their feud.

The Dogs and Death Riders vs. Conglomeration and The Bang Bang Gang

Gabe Kidd, Claudio Castagnoli, Daniel Garcia and Wheeler Yuta teamed up with Clark Connors and David Finlay to take on Roderick Strong, Kyle O'Reilly, Orange Cassidy, Jay White, Austin and Colten Gunn.

Whenever you have this many people in one match, it's going to end up being pure mayhem at some point, especially with these 12 men involved. It took less than a minute before everyone started coming in to fight without tags.

Even without a lot of structure, matches like this always end up being entertaining in AEW because everyone involved contributes to the fun. The Dogs and Death Riders were able to get the victory.

Result: Dogs and Death Riders defeated Conglomeration and Bang Bang Gang

The first in the Best of 5 series between FTR and The Motor City Machine Guns closed out the Tailgate Brawl pre-show. As usual, Stokely Hathaway was with Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler.

Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley received a nice welcome from the crowd for their first tag match on an AEW PPV. This is a match a lot of people have been looking forward to for quite some time, and they did not waste time before picking up the pace.

This was a fantastic display of the skill of both teams, but they still left room to grow in future encounters. The match ran more than 15 minutes past the end of the pre-show and into the main PPV. They had a lot of time to work, but when it was all over, Shelley and Sabin got the win to go up 1-0 in the series.

Result: Motor City Machine Guns defeated FTR

It was nice to see Willow out there with The Conglomeration.

White was only just cleared to compete again as of today.

Paul Wight putting over Claudio's strength is appropriate since Claudio slammed him over the top rope to win WWE's first Andre Memorial Battle Royal in 2014.

Mercedes Moné vs. Thekla (Women's World Championship)

The first official match on the main card saw Mercedes Moné put her women's world title on the line against Thekla.

The CEO actually came close to getting Thekla into her trademark submission early in the match, but The Toxic Spider used her flexibility to escape and taunt the champion at the same time.

The first half of this match was good, but they were definitely pacing themselves. They took more time to sell big moments, and they weren't rushing from spot to spot because they knew they had time.

This was much more about telling a story than trying to pack in as many moves as possible, and it worked to its benefit because anyone would have had a hard time following FTR and MCMG.

These two worked very well together and delivered a strong performance. This was just as good as the tag match that preceded it on the show, but for completely different reasons. The CEO prevailed in the end and hit the Moneymaker for the pin.

Mercedes always has great gear, but whoever made it for this show did especially great work. Thekla's jacket was awesome, too.

Thekla called the crowd "Dumb b-----s" and still got a pop. That's when you know you're over with the fans.

The way Mercedes kind of tossed Thekla to release the surfboard stretch was cool.

Updated 2026 AEW WrestleDream Card and Predictions for Match Order

Two different generations collided for the third time when Jericho took on Wayne. Both men had won against the other, so this was the rubber match in their feud to determine who would come out on top.

The crowd was heavily in Jericho's corner. It was singing his music for a few seconds after it had stopped playing, and he was getting Y2J chants before anything happened.

Nick slapped him and spat in his face, so Jericho spat back and then punched him to get the action started. Chris took a moment to have some fun with Paul Wight on commentary before slamming Wayne onto the steel steps.

The early minutes of this match felt like Jericho trying to teach his young opponent a lesson, but once Wayne had the upper hand, he stayed on the veteran while still taunting him at every turn.

This feud has been good for both men. It has given Nick a spotlight against a former world champion, and it's allowed Jericho to have some of the best matches he has had in AEW in quite some time.

The 21-year-old managed to kick out of the Codebreaker and escaped The Walls of Jericho. He took the low road and spat a liquid in Jericho's eyes, but it failed to get him the win. He tried a couple of low blows, but Jericho revealed he was wearing a cup to block them, which is something every wrestler should do at this point.

Y2J hit a low blow of his own, but then Wayne rolled him up for the pin out of nowhere. He grabbed a mic and bragged about winning as a little pyro went off on the stage.

The ring announcer read a prepared intro for Wayne that he obviously wrote himself. It did a good job getting him a little heat.

It looked like they spit gum at each other at the start, which was probably better because it was easier to see on camera than saliva.

Wayne's moonsault to the floor was great.

The Young Bucks vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight (Tag Team Championships)

The tag titles were on the line when Nick and Matt Jackson defended the belts against Knight and Fletcher of The Don Callis Family. Callis sat with the commentary team to watch from ringside.

There is no denying the skill of everyone involved in this bout. The Bucks are one of the most celebrated tag teams of this generation, and both members of the opposing team have had a lot of success in AEW before either man has had his 30th birthday.

They could have put on a fun match without even putting in much effort, but the fact that they were all trying hard to make this entertaining led to a very enjoyable outing.

Love them or hate them, The Young Bucks know how to put on an exciting performance. When you give them two young guys as athletic as Knight and Fletcher, you have the recipe for a match that would steal the show on most cards.

This match continued the string of strong performances we have gotten on this PPV so far. They really packed a lot of different near-fall scenarios into this one, but it made the crowd get on its feet for the final few minutes.

The ending may have been predictable with the Bucks retaining, but that didn't make the journey to get there any less fun. The Bucks pinned Knight with the BTE Trigger to retain the titles.

Result: The Young Bucks defeated Fletcher and Knight

It was kind of interesting to see Knight and Fletcher have separate entrances instead of coming out as a unit. At least they coordinated their gear.

The crowd was chanting "F--k Don Callis."

It's kind of funny how the announcers tried to position Fletcher as a singles star who happens to be in a tag match when he spent a lot of his career in a team with Davis as Aussie Open.

Callis interfered while on commentary by raking Matt's eyes.

The TBS title was on the line in the next match when Persephone had to face three different challengers in Hyan, Luna and Aminata.

The three challengers decided to work together to take out Persephone early on, but it didn't take long for those alliances to crumble.

This felt like a very fresh match for AEW. A year ago, these four women were either much lower on the card or not signed yet, so seeing them all in this position on a PPV shows how much the women's division has grown in 2026.

This bout gave all four wrestlers a chance to shine at different times, but it felt like Aminata was the only challenger who might have had a chance to win the belt from Persephone.

This was a very physical encounter that is likely to leave all four women with a few bruises. Persephone retained her title by pinning Hyan with a moonsault.

The rise of Queen Aminata has been a lot of fun to watch.

Persephone trying to complain to the ref about everyone teaming up on her was funny.

Maya World and Britt Baker came out with Hyan and Persephone's entrances, but neither remained at ringside.

The powerbomb Luna took on the floor did not look fun.

The way Aminata hit a dropkick to Hyan while she was in a chair looked brutal.

Persephone's moonsault came nowhere near hitting Hyan and Luna. It was an unfortunate moment in an otherwise great bout.

We went right into the next title bout with Andrade defending the National Championship against Ciampa.

They started by testing each other with some chest chops, but they were throwing punches within a few seconds. Ciampa prevented Andrade from taking off his pants, much to the chagrin of some fans in the crowd.

This show had already delivered some incredible wrestling, so Ciampa and El Idolo were under some pressure to continue that trend, but these are two guys who have always been capable of great things.

While the match was good, it did not feel like we got the best either man can give. It might have had something to do with how it was paced, but whatever it was, it felt like they were holding back until the second half.

Andrade only had his pants halfway off when he hit his signature double moonsault. It felt like once he got them off, that is when the pace picked up. Ciampa pretending to pin Andrade's pants, only for them to kick out, was the funniest part of the match.

There was a moment when it looked like Ciampa may win with help from the belt, but Andrade beat him to the punch and used it against him to get the win.

AEW accidentally used the international title graphic at the beginning of the match.

Andrade got his old entrance music back.

Ciampa posing for a pic with his daughter was a nice moment.

Ciampa taking off his trunks to reveal different trunks was hilarious.

Swerve Strickland and New Level vs. Hangman and Brodido (Trios Championships)

The Trios Championships were defended in a two-out-of-three falls match with Swerve, Kofi and Austin Creed taking on Hangman, Bandido and Brody King.

Creed and Bandido started the match with a pretty simple exchange. It almost felt like they were trying to pace themselves because they knew this was a marathon, not a sprint.

They went for quite some time before Kofi scored the first fall by pinning Bandido. They gave him no time to recover, but Hangman prevented Swerve from getting a second fall right away.

Bandido ended up evening the score by pinning Creed, so it was 1-1 heading into the final portion of the match. As much fun as this was, it felt a little disorganized at times, but not in the chaotic way we're used to with these trios bouts.

The story between Hangman and Swerve dominated most of the story being told, and they did a good job keeping the tension high. In a bit of a shocking outcome, Bandido ended up pinning Swerve to regain the trios titles.

Swerve did not want him and New Level to hand over the belts, but they did eventually. New Level handed them to Brodido first, and then Swerve dropped his in front of Hangman.

Result: Hangman and Brodido won the Trios Championships

The crowd popped bit as soon as Hangman and Swerve for their hands on each other.

King is one of those guys who looks like he should be a heel, but he works so well as a babyface.

Creed slapping King right before King destroyed him was a fun moment.

Swerve's double stomp to Hangman hit him in the head more than the chest.

Ilja Dragunov was introduced as the newest member of All Elite Wrestling to a big ovation from the crowd. He interacted with the crowd a bit, but he did not speak, so his first promo will likely happen on Dynamite this week.

The penultimate match of the night saw Moxley put the continental title on the line against Davis of the DCF. Davis pinned Mox in a match earlier this week, so he was hoping to carry that momentum into this bout.

Mox made the mistake of trying a shoulder tackle against Dunkzilla, so when it was brushed off, he had to rethink his strategy. For the first few minutes, it seemed like Davis had an answer for everything the champion tried.

Moxley was busted wide open near his eye and blood began pouring out as Davis stayed on him and tried to open the wound even more.

This match didn't try to match the level of excitement of previous bouts by going for a bunch of high-risk spots. They wanted this to be the most violent encounter of the night, and they succeeded.

The ref warned Moxley that he might call the match if he did not make it back to the ring. Moxley looked like he was thinking of giving up until Marina Shafir and Daniel Garcia showed up in the crowd to give him a pep talk.

It felt like Mox was using his real grief over the loss of Pac as part of the story in this match, and it made things that much more intense. Once he got a boost from his friend, the champ started to take over.

This was a tremendous combination of hard-hitting action and storytelling in the ring. After a brutal fight that left both men a bloody mess, Mox choked Davis out to retain his title.

The Death Riders continuing to pay tribute to Pac is great.

For a big, surly guy, Davis looks like he takes good care of his beard.

Moxley's wound was quite the gusher. Even Davis was covered in his blood after a few minutes.

The piledriver on the apron was a cool spot.

The main event of WrestleDream was the first AEW Clockwork Carnage match. This bout combined elements of a gauntlet, a scramble match and a Battle Royal.

The first two competitors to enter the ring were the defending champion, Ospreay, and Takeshita. Another person joined the match every three minutes. Anyone pinned before everyone was in the ring was eliminated. Whoever was left once everyone was in the ring had 15 minutes to get as many falls as possible.

Bailey was the third man to join the match, Ricochet was the fourth, Allin was fifth, Okada was out sixth, Copeland was the seventh to arrive, and the final competitor was Joe.

With Bailey and Takeshita eliminated, there were only six men in the final phase. Joe scored the first point, and Ricochet scored the second shortly after. Okada wasn't far behind with the third fall.

The falls started to come quickly, with Allin and Ospreay jumping out to a lead with two each by the time five minutes had passed.

This was a unique concept for a match. While it's tough to say if the format is something people will get invested in, the eight men involved all did a good job of making the first one enjoyable.

Ospreay, Copeland, Joe and Allin each had two falls by the time we got to a minute left on the clock. Ospreay scored his third fall on Copeland with two seconds left on the clock to win and retain his title.

Copeland shook his hand, but he made it clear he was still coming for the title.

Bailey's United Empire gear looked cool.

Takeshita did not hold back when he slapped Ricochet's bald head.

You don't often see someone superplex two people at once, but Takeshita made it look easy.

Bailey was eliminated before Copeland arrived. Okada eliminated Takeshita before Joe arrived.

Joe doing the walkaway spot during Ricochet's suicide dive was great.

It was nice to have the graphic at the bottom of the screen so keep track of the results.

Whenever the build to an AEW PPV is a little underwhelming, the talent end up making it one of the best shows of the year, and this was no exception.

Every single match on the card delivered in one way or another. We saw just about everything on this show, from high-flying stunts to bloody brawling.

The three women's matches stood out as being especially strong, but Thekla and Mercedes had one of the best performances on the entire show.

The tag and trios title bouts were probably the biggest highlights of the night, but you would be hard-pressed to name a single weak match.

The first Clockwork Carnage was enjoyable, but time will tell if the format catches on in AEW.

articles.title: Mercedes Mone Beats Thekla to Retain AEW Women's World Title at WrestleDream 2026
articles.summary: Mercedes Moné defeated Thekla to retain the AEW Women's World Championship at WrestleDream on Saturday.
articles.body:
Mercedes Moné defeated Thekla to retain the AEW Women's World Championship at WrestleDream on Saturday.

Updated 2026 AEW WrestleDream Card and Predictions for Match Order

Near the end of the match, Moné used her mask to attack Thekla.

She then tried to land the Mone Maker, but Thekla countered and rolled up Moné for a pin attempt.

However, Moné couldn't be held back for long. She evaded Thekla's attempt to hit Blackout and countered with the Moné Maker for the win.

After falling short in multiple attempts previously, Moné finally became AEW women's world champion for the first time in August at All In when she beat Willow Nightingale.

The CEO suffered a broken nose during that physical bout, which kept her out of action for the next month.

With Mercedes not cleared to compete at All Out last month, Thekla and Nightingale faced off in a No. 1 contender's match for the right to challenge for the AEW women's world title at WrestleDream.

Thekla was victorious, and she gained retribution in the process, as Willow was the one who ended her 165-day reign as AEW women's champ.

Moné returned to action on the Sept. 30 episode of Dynamite, which paid tribute to Pac, losing to Marina Shafir, Thunder Rosa and Hyan in a six-woman tag team match.

Mercedes bounced back in her next outing, though, beating Queen Aminata to retain the AEW women's world title on the Oct. 6 Grand Slam France edition of Dynamite.

With that, Moné locked in her spot on the WrestleDream card and cemented a highly anticipated clash with Thekla.

Since Thekla had a lengthy title reign with All In approaching, many assumed she would face Mercedes then, but Willow's title win threw a wrench into those plans.

Fans had to wait a bit longer than anticipated for Moné vs. Thekla, but they delivered, and The CEO prevailed.

articles.title: Sebastián Fundora retiene el título con nocaut en el último segundo ante un aguerrido Ermal Hadribeaj
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense retiene su corona, pero las dudas no desaparecen
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense retiene su corona, pero las dudas no desaparecen
articles.body: Las Vegas, Nevada fueron testigos de la pelea entre Sebastián Fundora y Ermal Hadribeaj por el campeonato mundial superwélter del Consejo Mundia de Boxeo (CMB) en la que los dos pugilistas tuvieron sus momentos en el cuadrilátero, siendo un dominio alterno en el que estaba latente la posibilidad de un nocaut por el poder de la pegada. Y es que el tiro de gracia de Sebastián Fundora llegó en los últimos segundos del doceavo round por lo que existía la duda de si iba a contar como nocaut o no, pero de acuerdo con la decisión final, el golpe llegó al minuto 2:59 por lo que se confirmó la victoria del estadounidense por KO. En el boxeo un segundo puede marcar la diferencia, por eso muchas veces se usa la frase de "lo salvó la campana", pero en el caso de Ermal Hadribeaj no fue el caso, pues cuando parecía que todo se iba a la decisión de los jueces entró en el último intercambio de golpes y no pudo aguantar a terminar la pelea y cayó. Sin embargo, por momentos la duda se adueñó de la arena porque no se sabía qué sería la decisión oficial por lo que se revisó el cronómetro y el golpe de Sebastián Fundora entró en el último segundo y así ha sumado un nuevo nocaut en su carrera como pugilista aunque esto no ha terminado con los cuestionamientos a su pelea. Sebastián Fundora, boxeador estadounidense, ha sido fuertemente cuestionado por los analistas de boxeo y seguidores de este deporte pues consideran que no muestra todo su potencial cuando sube a los cuadriláteros pese a haber ganado su última pelea por nocaut. Y es que justo uno de los señalamientos es que aguanta mucho a sus rivales ayudandose de su altura y distancia que puede tomar para entrar al intercambio en la recta final y el claro ejemplo es su pelea contra Ermal Hadribeaj que se animó hasta el último round a entrar de lleno al intercambio.

articles.title: Mike Malott Flattens Joaquin Buckley With Devastating Knee Strike at UFC Edmonton
articles.summary: Mike Malott won his 5th straight inside the Octagon as he knocked out Joaquin Buckley in the main event of UFC Edmonton.
articles.body:
Mike Malott made sure he had the last laugh against Joaquin Buckley at UFC Edmonton. The Canadian delivered a brutal second-round knockout in the main event at Rogers Place in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, sending the hometown crowd into a frenzy.

The fans witnessed a violent finish as their hometown hero put Buckley away at the 2:32 mark of Round 2 on Saturday night. It was the kind of highlight that instantly grabs attention, and Malott couldn't have picked a better stage to deliver it.

There was plenty of tension heading into fight week, with Buckley taking an unusually cold approach to the matchup. He refused to shake Dana White's hand during the face-offs, declined to speak to backstage interviewers, and even refused to touch gloves when the fight began.

The opening round was relatively calm, with both fighters taking their time to find their range. They traded sharp kicks and hooks, but neither managed to take control for long. That changed dramatically in the second round.

Buckley came out swinging, marching forward with a flurry of punches. Malott responded by clinching him against the fence, potentially looking to slow him down and wear him out.

Once the action returned to the center of the Octagon, Malott unleashed the shot that changed everything. What initially looked like a body kick turned into a devastating knee to Buckley's face. The impact sent Buckley's mouthpiece flying and left him unconscious.

Buckley was throwing a punch at the same time, and his forward momentum carried him onto all fours as he fell. Malott followed up with a heavy punch, leaving his opponent face-down on the canvas and bringing the fight to a brutal end.

The victory marked Malott's fifth consecutive win, with three of those victories coming by finish . He most recently stopped Gilbert Burns in the main event of UFC Winnipeg, and this latest performance could put him in the conversation for a major step up in competition.

Things are going in the opposite direction for Buckley , who has now suffered three straight defeats after previously losing to Kamaru Usman and Sean Brady. After the loss to Malott, "New Mansa" will need to regroup before thinking about his next move.

Mike Malott Calls for a Top-10 Opponent After UFC Edmonton Win

Malott wasted little time making his ambitions clear after the knockout. During his post-fight interview with Paul Felder, the Canadian called for a matchup against a ranked contender, making it clear that he believes he belongs among the division's best.

He said, "Guys, I might be soft-spoken, but I'm f*cking hard-hitting. I see a lot of dangerous guys in the top-10. Top-10 at the very least, maybe top-five."

It's a confident callout from Malott, and his performance against Buckley gives him a strong argument for facing tougher competition next.

With UFC 336 officially announced for Toronto's Scotiabank Arena on January 30, Malott could have another opportunity to fight in front of his Canadian fans. A matchup against a top contender on home soil would be an ideal next step for the rising welterweight, especially after delivering one of the night's most memorable finishes in Edmonton.

articles.title: Dana White shrugs off UFC not re-signing 7-0 Farid Basharat: 'There's definitely a reason'
articles.summary: Basharat went 7-0 during his UFC tenure but was controversially not offered a new contract after completing his previous deal with the promotion.
articles.body:
UFC CEO Dana White addressed his promotion's decision not to re-sign undefeated bantamweight Farid Basharat following Saturday night's UFC Edmonton event .

Basharat (16-0) went 7-0 during his UFC tenure but was controversially not offered a new contract this week after completing his previous deal with the promotion.

Asked about the decision at Saturday's post-fight press conference, White said there are several reasons why the UFC might choose not to re-sign a fighter and alluded to potential issues behind the scenes with the promotion's matchmakers.

"I mean, this isn't the first time this has happened," White said. "And either guys aren't good to deal with and the matchmakers don't want to deal with them, which could be turning down fights or whatever the reasoning is."

"If you're 16-0 with seven wins in the UFC, and don't get re-signed," he continued, "there's definitely a reason."

White declined to further elaborate on why the UFC opted not to offer Basharat a new contract. He also declined to confirm whether any of the circumstances he mentioned applied to Basharat specifically.

Basharat, 29, said this week that he was never offered another contract or opponent after his final UFC win, and denied turning down any fights during his time with the promotion.

The Afghan-born bantamweight earned his way to the UFC through the promotion's Contender Series in 2022, and made his official promotional debut in 2023. Six of his seven Octagon victories came in decisions. He did not win a single post-fight bonus during his four years with the company.

Basharat's final UFC appearance ultimately came in a July decision win over John Garza.

articles.title: Will Ospreay, Mercedes Moné and Real Winners and Losers of AEW WrestleDream Match Card
articles.summary: The 2026 edition of WrestleDream featured championship and a first-time special match for the AEW Men's World Championship, airing from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida.
articles.body:
The 2026 edition of WrestleDream featured championship and a first-time special match for the AEW Men's World Championship, airing from Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida.

Will Ospreay overcame the odds in Clockwork Carnage to retain his AEW Men's World Championship while Mercedes Moné defeated her top rival Thekla to successfully defend her gold.

Swerve Strickland and New Level fell to Hangman Adam Page and Brodido. Jon Moxley pushed through the pain to retain the Continental Championship against Mark Davis.

This was only the foundation of a fun night of All Elite Wrestling action. For all the real winners and losers from WrestleDream, keep reading.

It has been an odd start for Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley. The Motor City Machine Guns have slowly found their footing in AEW, barely appearing to date.

In some ways, their match with FTR was the true introduction to AEW for MCMG, who finally got to show off what they could do.

It was a long battle against Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler that started on the Tailgate Brawl and bled 15 minutes into the main show.

While capturing the first win in a Best of 5 series was nice, it was even more important that Sabin and Shelley looked like one of the best tag teams in AEW right now.

The best bet is that this series will lead to The Young Bucks facing MCMG. By the end of that match, AEW fans will chose if they have bought into this veteran team.

This was a great start to selling the unfamiliar fans on what they can do.

Mercedes Moné continues to show she is one of the best wrestlers in the world, delivering matches every time out that rival even the top men in AEW right now.

She brought out the best match from Thekla of her run in AEW. It is rare that heel vs. heel works this well, but because of the personality and charisma of both women, both were supported through this battle.

This was a definitive win for The CEO, who stands far and above the rest of the women's roster right now.

Anyone could step up to Moné next week, but at least until Toni Storm returns, no one else is a clear candidate to dethrone the Women's world champion.

What most matters for The CEO will be the company building strong stories around her. Who is going to be built to step up to The CEO's level?

The biggest winner of WrestleDream was the man in the least anticipated match of the show.

After Nick Wayne defeated Jericho at Grand Slam: France, it looked likely Y2J would clearly establish himself as the better man at the pay-per-view.

Instead, Jericho let Wayne show out at WrestleDream and find a way to defeat Y2J a second time and seal a victory in this rivalry.

Hopefully, Wayne can move on from this angle after this win and begin a true ascent up the roster.

At just 21 years old, The Prodigy could quickly become one of the defining stars of the next era in AEW, running with these two wins over a legend to gold and glory.

Updated 2026 AEW WrestleDream Card and Predictions for Match Order

Don Callis took a big risk in putting Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight against The Young Bucks, and it did not pay off.

Much like the other tag teams Callis has assembled, this alliance fell apart when it mattered most, which allowed Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson to take them down.

This tag title match also cost one or both of Fletcher and Knight a spot in the Clockwork Carnage match, which meant Callis had just one client in the contest, Kazuchika Okada.

The Rainmaker did not win that match nor did Mark Davis take the Continental Championship, so The Callis Family left WrestleDream with no extra gold or a clear path to more gold in the near-future.

The Family is the least dangerous it has been in a while, and it is more likely than ever that The Family might lose more members, especially a frustrated Protostar.

Queen Aminata quite nearly pinned Persephone and won her first AEW gold if it was not for the intervention of Hyan.

This was the latest heartbreaker for Aminata, who still has yet to win either AEW or Ring of Honor gold despite her standing as one of the company's best women.

Of every woman in this 4-Way battle, Aminata was the most deserving of taking that title given her longevity with AEW.

That win may still be in the cards, but for now, she must wait another day for an opportunity one on one against Persephone.

When Persephone captured the TBS Championship while still the CMLL world women's champion, the possibility this would be a short reign was high.

Her constant responsibilities for CMLL though have not gotten in the way of Persephone working one of the most hectic schedules of any woman in AEW.

This would have been an easy time to move the title without costing the CMLL champion a pinfall or submission.

Instead, Persephone has now technically defeated all the major rivals to her TBS Championship.

It should be interesting to see how AEW follows this win up as it looks more likely than ever that she is at least getting to Winter is Coming in Monterrey, Mexico with two titles.

Tommaso Ciampa came into AEW by immediately establishing his desire to be a champion. His short TNT Championship reign made clear he was going to win many titles.

Since that time though, The Psycho Killer has struggled to find his way back to gold. He fell short in his rivalry with Jericho and suffered multiple championship losses.

This National Championship opportunity against Andrade El Ídolo might have been the last opportunity for Ciampa to capture gold again in 2026, and he fell short.

As great as the match was, El Ídolo did not need to win this to keep his momentum, especially as he continues to carry the Casino Gauntlet contract for a guaranteed world title shot.

Where does The Psycho Killer go from here? He has consistently delivered on big stages, but he cannot keep getting spots like this only to lose.

Swerve Strickland made a firm statement by bringing in Kofi and Austin Creed to take the World Trios Championships from Hangman Adam Page, Brody King and Bandido.

He wanted to take everything away from The Cowboy, but it seems to have only motivated Hangman further, who rebounded with Brodido to take the gold back.

The Mogul saw himself to be the lesser man when it mattered most, and New Level saw the pettiness that drives Swerve take over.

What will become of Swerve's alliance with New Level? Only time will tell, but Kofi and Creed clearly did not agree with his attitude.

This should free up New Level to go after The Young Bucks, which is what AEW fans are most clambering for, leaving Swerve alone again.

Hangman Adam Page, Brody King and Bandido have reclaimed the World Trios Championships, and no one was happier than the ROH world champion.

Bandido took the first fall in this contest and rallied his team to make the comeback. He kept his team focused and drove their energy.

It was an ultimate babyface performance even before he hit both Kofi and Creed with a Double Diving Spanish Fly and pinned Swerve for the deciding fall.

This was Bandido's third AEW title win, and he recently passed the day limit for the most time as ROH world champion at 710 days.

It is clear that the luchador is a made star and will be one of AEW's top stars going forward, even if he remains a trios performer first into 2027.

The Mad Dragon has arrived in AEW. Ilja Dragunov made his first entrance in the company to a wild pop under the same name he made popular on a worldwide stage with WWE.

While he delivered many times in the ring with WWE, he was never treated as a big deal on Raw or SmackDown in the way he was in his introduction at WrestleDream.

The road is still uncertain in front of Dragunov. He was not given an immediate feud, so how AEW sees him is still not fully established.

It looks good to start though as a fresh path forward is exactly what The Mad Dragon needed.

It may not look like it was a successful night for Mark Davis, given he lost in his bid for the Continental Championship, but this was a career performance against Jon Moxley.

The two battled in the most emotional contest of the night, driving home that Mox was fighting through his own pain in recently losing his close friend Pac.

By the close, Mox and Davis both had spilled enough blood to permanently stain the canvas.

This match solidified Davis as one of the scariest heel monsters in wrestling right now and will likely lead to him capturing more accolades soon.

Losers: Konosuke Takeshita and "Speedball" Mike Bailey

Someone had to get eliminated before the final stretch of Clockwork Carnage, but it was disappointing to lose Konosuke Takeshita and "Speedball" MIke Bailey.

Both are great competitors that deserve a major spotlight. They guided the first stage of the action as the second and third participants, and both did not go down easily.

The Alpha especially should eventually be in the world title picture in AEW, though he will need to collide with Kazuchika Okada again before that.

Speedball is an impressive athlete that always over-delivers with opportunities. If he is out of the world title picture, he should at least be gearing up for another Continental Classic run.

Will Ospreay came up with the idea of Clockwork Carnage then after one run in Pro-Wrestling: EVE, he was comfortable running it on a major AEW PPV.

This main event was not the best contest of the night, but it was still an exciting home stretch to WrestleDream that showed why AEW should run this concept more.

Ospreay tested the time limit and ran it all the way down to the wire to protect his AEW Men's World Championship.

At the end, he also has established multiple big names as future challengers, especially Adam Copeland and Samoa Joe, which would make for exciting PPV main events.

Whatever comes next, Ospreay has certainly showed he can steer the ship in interesting and exciting directions.

articles.title: Will Ospreay Wins 1st-Ever AEW Clockwork Carnage to Retain AEW Title at WrestleDream 2026
articles.summary: Will Ospreay won AEW's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay won AEW's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.

Ospreay prevailed in a unique, eight-man match that also included Samoa Joe, "Speedball" Mike Bailey, Adam Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet and Darby Allin.

Here's a look at the rules and how it all went down.

Takeshita eliminated Bailey with Raging Fire.

However, Okada knocked out Takeshita with the Rainmaker.

The scoring period began after Samoa Joe entered the match as the eighth and final competitor. He got the first point after hitting Allin with the Muscle Buster.

Ricochet got a point too, hitting Allin with a lateral press.

Okada got on the scoreboard when he landed the Rainmaker on Copeland.

The champion got his first point when he executed the Styles Clash on Ricochet, but Allin got his point with a Coffin Drop on Ospreay.

At this juncture, five of the six remaining wrestlers had a point apiece, with Copeland being the lone exception.

Allin took the lead when he pinned Copeland following La Casita. Ospreay evened the score at two points, though, when he pinned Allin following Hidden Blade.

Samoa Joe got his second point when he made Ospreay tap with the Coquina Clutch.

Copeland then made things awfully interesting with back-to-back points on spears to Samoa Joe and then Ricochet.

With a minute left, Copeland, Allin, Samoa Joe and Ospreay had two points each. Okada and Ricochet had one point apiece. Copeland was in position to win the match after hitting a spear on Okada, but Ospreay broke up the pin by hitting Copeland with the Hidden Blade and then pinning him with just a few seconds on the clock.

That was good enough for the win. Afterward, Copeland and Ospreay had a heated exchange.

The match type was conceived in Pro-Wrestling: EVE—a promotion in which Ospreay works behind the scenes in the United Kingdom.

Ospreay brought the stipulation to AEW, willingly putting his world title on the line against seven of the best challengers the company has to offer.

A series of qualifying matches were held leading up to WrestleDream, starting off with a de facto qualifier when Ospreay beat Okada at the Grand Slam France edition of Dynamite to retain the AEW World Championship.

Additionally, Joe defeated Jack Perry, Bailey took down Lee Moriarty, Copeland beat Josh Alexander, Takeshita topped Brian Cage, Okada got the better of Myron Reed, Ricochet outlasted Ace Austin, and Allin triumphed over Hechicero to qualify.

With such a stacked field in the Clockwork Carnage match, Ospreay was seemingly in legitimate danger of seeing his title reign end after less than two months.

However, Ospreay was clearly motivated to win the match he helped create, especially with it taking place on a big stage for the first time.

That is exactly what Ospreay did, as he outlasted seven hungry challengers to conquer Clockwork Carnage and remain AEW world champion.

articles.title: Dubois vs Wardley 2: What next for heavyweight division after Dubois win?
articles.summary: After world champion Daniel Dubois' emphatic win over Fabio Wardley, what's next for the heavyweight division?
articles.body:
Daniel Dubois' demolition of Fabio Wardley has strengthened his position among the heavyweight elite.

The 29-year-old needed only two rounds to stop his British rival at London's O2 Arena, retaining his title with a performance far more emphatic than their thrilling first encounter in May.

Dubois can now turn his attention towards unification and some of boxing's biggest names.

Meanwhile, Oleksandr Usyk is approaching retirement, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally preparing to meet and a new group of world champions are looking to establish themselves.

So what is next for the heavyweight division?

Who is next for Dubois - and where does Wardley go?

IBF champion Filip Hrgovic made his intentions clear, entering the ring after Dubois' victory, with both keen on a rematch.

Dubois stopped the Croatian in June 2024, but Hrgovic has since rebuilt his reputation, claiming the vacant IBF title with victory over British prospect Moses Itauma in August.

But Hrgovic, 34, has Cuba's Frank Sanchez waiting as a mandatory challenger.

Promoter Frank Warren is working towards staging Hrgovic's first defence in Croatia early next year, potentially delaying a reunion with Dubois.

The biggest financial prize for Dubois could be a meeting with the winner of Fury and Joshua's December showdown.

"All those names are there to do a unification fight next year and that's what we'll be working on," Warren said.

Wardley, meanwhile, has shown he can compete at world level, but the manner of Saturday's defeat exposed a gulf in technical ability.

A return against a lower-ranked opponent could help restore confidence, but questions remain over whether Wardley can make the adjustments needed to challenge the division's elite again.

Fury v Joshua - finally, but what happens afterwards?

After years of negotiations and false starts, Fury and Joshua are finally scheduled to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on a card that begins on 11 December, with the main event expected in the early hours of 12 December.

The Netflix-streamed contest has demonstrated its extraordinary commercial appeal, with about 80,000 tickets selling out within an hour.

Warren says the vacant WBA 'super' title will be at stake, potentially opening the door to unification fights in 2027.

However, WBA 'regular' champion Murat Gassiev has questioned the decision and called for the winner to face him.

That appears unlikely to be a priority for either Briton, with both reportedly set to earn close to $100m (£75m) in December.

A rematch would offer another enormous payday, particularly if the first encounter is close or controversial, but a one-sided defeat could push the loser towards retirement.

Germany's Agit Kabayel has built one of the strongest records in the division.

The unbeaten 34-year-old has stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov, Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang, but remains a relatively unfamiliar name to casual boxing fans.

Kabayel, elevated to WBC champion when Usyk vacated, makes his first defence against Albania's Nelson Hysa on 28 November.

A unification fight against Dubois in 2027 could provide the opportunity to become a much bigger name in the sport.

Usyk's final fight - and what about Verhoeven and Wilder?

Usyk's decision to vacate the WBA, WBC and IBF titles in June means the unbeaten Ukrainian can call the shots over the final chapter of his career.

The pound-for-pound star, who defeated former kickboxing world champion Rico Verhoeven in May, has indicated he wants one final contest before retirement.

Dutchman Verhoeven exceeded expectations before suffering a controversial 11th-round stoppage defeat, and wants a rematch.

Verhoeven says he has accepted an offer to face Deontay Wilder on the Fury-Joshua undercard, although the American has yet to agree and has also been linked with cruiserweight Jai Opetaia.

Wilder previously emerged as a contender for Usyk's farewell, but negotiations appear to have stalled.

A third meeting between Usyk and Fury has also been mooted.

But having already beaten Fury, Joshua and Dubois twice apiece, how much more does Usyk have to prove?

Itauma's charge towards a world title was halted when he suffered his first professional defeat against Hrgovic.

Itauma, 21, is expected to return in January, with Warren promising credible opposition rather than a straightforward confidence-building contest.

The priority will be developing the stamina, pacing and tactical patience required over 12 rounds before pursuing another world title opportunity.

A rematch with Hrgovic remains a longer-term possibility, but there is little need to rush with time firmly on Itauma's side.

What else is happening on the global and domestic scene?

American Jarrell Miller remains highly ranked, while compatriots Jared Anderson and Richard Torrez Jr, an Olympic silver medallist, are rebuilding.

New Zealand's former world champion Joseph Parker is seeking a return after his provisional doping suspension was lifted in August.

Australia's Teremoana Teremoana has stopped all 12 professional opponents within two rounds, while Uzbekistan's two-time Olympic champion Bakhodir Jalolov extended his unbeaten record by beating Solomon Dacres on Saturday.

In Britain, Derek Chisora, 42, is considering another comeback and says he expects to face WBA 'regular' champion Gassiev in December.

British champion Richard Riakporhe is pursuing world honours after moving up from cruiserweight, while former cruiserweight world champion Lawrence Okolie is targeting a return after reaching an agreement with the WBC over an adverse drugs test finding.

David Adeleye, Dave Allen, Johnny Fisher and Frazer Clarke remain on the domestic scene, while Leo Atang, 19, and Ireland's Adam Olaniyan, 20, are emerging talents.

With Usyk, Fury and Joshua approaching the ends of their careers, the heavyweight division is entering a new era.

There is no shortage of potential big fights, but bringing the champions together before mandatory obligations, rematches and boxing politics get in the way could prove the greatest challenge.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois wants Oleksandr Usyk trilogy fight after Fabio Wardley victory: 'We're coming out on top this time!'
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois won his rematch with Fabio Wardley at the O2 on Saturday to defend the WBO heavyweight world title in devastating style; Dubois took out Wardley in two rounds and now wants championship unifications; The Londoner welcomes a trilogy fight with unbeaten great Oleksandr Usyk
articles.body:
Twice Dubois has boxed the imperious Ukrainian, and twice Usyk, an unbeaten and two-time undisputed champion at heavyweight, has stopped the Londoner.

But after a stunning two-round victory in his rematch with Fabio Wardley on Saturday, Dubois is convinced he has reached a new level and can beat Usyk.

No heavyweight, Dubois is adamant, can stand up to the punches he hit Wardley with.

"No. Fabio's got a great chin. He's known for taking punishment but I was going through him. I just had to pull myself back and reset. I want to know who's next!" Dubois declared.

He would welcome a potential trilogy fight with Usyk. "Definitely, definitely, I'd love that," Dubois said. "We're coming out on top this time. We've made our mistakes and we're coming out on top."

Promoter Frank Warren said: "Daniel in my opinion he's not the same fighter he was even a year ago. He's a totally different fighter now.

"When he's doing what he's doing at his best, you've got to be some fighter to be standing and being able to take those shots. He's a tremendous puncher. When he gets you in trouble, you are in trouble. He's a good finisher."

Usyk vacated all the world titles he held, allowing Dubois to claim the WBO belt ahead of his first fight with Wardley, Filip Hrgovic to pick up the IBF strap after beating Moses Itauma, and Agit Kabayel to be elevated to WBC heavyweight world champion.

Next year Dubois is looking to add more championships to his collection. "I've heard talk about Kabayel but I'll fight whoever's next in line. Whoever pays the most cash," Dubois said.

Promoter Frank Warren thinks it will take 18 months for a new undisputed champion to be crowned, but expects a wave of heavyweight unifications to get under way in next year.

"I think it'll happen in about 18 months because of the timings of it all," Warren said. "We will make them as soon as we can, I expect in the first quarter we'll have at least one of those unifications on. If we get it on, somebody's going to be holding two belts.

"Filip's got a mandatory against [Frank] Sanchez," Warren noted. "We've got Agit, who's fighting in November in Germany and we've got Tyson [Fury] and AJ fighting in December [for the WBA 'super' title]. So they're all busy but we'll be out, don't worry about that.

"The good thing about it is everybody wants to fight. They're fighting men.

"We want the best fighting the best to find out who is the best," the promoter continued. "Get Usyk back in it.

"There's all sort of permutations. One thing for sure is 2027 is going to be a phenomenal year.

"[Dubois] wants the four belts. So do all the other guys. That's what's going to be so exciting."

articles.body: LONDON — Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight title with a brutal second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley on Saturday as their fight of the year rematch at the O2 Arena in London ended in a furious assault from the champion. There were 39 seconds of the round left when referee Steve Gray waved off the contest at the same time as the towel was thrown into the ring by Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison. Dubois was also punishing in the first round — he needed just 17 seconds to put fellow British boxer Wardley on the canvas with an overhand right. Resuming hostilities just five months after their first slugfest, Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) launched an all-out assault from the first bell and was rewarded with a destructive victory that issued a statement to his rivals in the division. “It was my time and it’s my era. I had bad intentions from the beginning,” Dubois told Britain’s Press Association. “We just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did.” Dubois had bloodied Wardley in an 11th-round stoppage victory in May to become a two-time heavyweight champion. Wardley dropped the former IBF champion just seconds into that fight in Manchester but never looked a threat to Dubois on Saturday. It was the second professional loss for Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KOs). “It’s never fun to lose, but it is what it is. The game is the game,” Wardley said. “I have always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there — the best in the business, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around — so there’s no shame in a loss when you’re testing yourself against the best.”

articles.title: Mallot noquea a Buckley y se convierte en el héroe del UFC Canadá
articles.standfirst: El peleador local dio un golpe sobre la mesa para seguir avanzando en la división de peso wélter
articles.summary: El peleador local dio un golpe sobre la mesa para seguir avanzando en la división de peso wélter
articles.body: El UFC Canadá de la pasada madrugada fue la consagración de Mike Mallot (15-2-1) como un serio peligro para la división de peso wélter. El ídolo local canadiense noqueó a Joaquín Buckley (21-9) en el segundo asalto con una brutal rodilla para dar un salto de gigante en la categoría y demostrar que ya está preparado para medirse a los grandes nombres de las 170 libras. Desde su llegada a la UFC en 2022, Mallot acumula ocho victorias y una derrota, pero sin duda esta ha sido la más importante y contundente. Buckley es uno de los mayores noqueadores de la categoría, y solo había perdido en esta división contra Sean Brady y Kamaru Usman. Sin embargo, en el segundo asalto se vio sorprendido por una patada a la cabeza del canadiense en la corta distancia que se acabó convirtiendo en una rodilla hacia su mandíbula que le apagó las luces. Además, Jasmine Jasudavicius (16-4) también hizo ponerse en pie al público local después de dominar a Erin Blanchfield (14-3) en el evento co estelar y dar un paso de gigante en la categoría de peso mosca femenino. Por si fuera poco, la peleadora canadiense lo logró dominando a la estadounidense en la pelea en suelo, su punto fuerte. Por otro lado, Cristian 'Púas' Pérez (16-2) debutó por la puerta grande en la UFC tras ganarse el contrato en las Dana White's Contender Series hace unas semanas. El peleador mexicano será un nombre muy a tener en cuenta en peso ligero, y dio prueba de ello noqueando a Kyle Nelson (17-8-1) en 27 segundos. Marc-André Barriault (18-11, 1NC) hizo lo propio con Kyle Daukaus (17-6, 1NC) en el primer asalto, y Timmy Cuamba (11-4) amargó el debut del canadiense Louis Jourdain (9-4) al someterlo en el segundo asalto. Mandel Nallo (15-4, 1NC) también pudo redimirse de su debut con derrota ante Jai Herbert dando otra alegría al público canadiense al noquear a Nate Landwehr (18-9) a base de patadas a las piernas, y con eso completó una cartelera estelar donde todas las peleas fueron finalizaciones menos una. Por si fuera poco, los siete combates de la cartelera preliminar también tuvieron un 100% de finalizaciones, dejando uno de los mejores eventos del año. Tanner Boser, Nick Galanti, Katlyn Chookagian o Chelsea Chandler fueron algunos de los grandes nombres de los primeros combates, donde hubo luces y sombras para los intereses locales. Lo que está claro es que la Ley de Murphy se sigue cumpliendo, y cuando hay un evento con pocas expectativas los dioses de las MMA nos regalan una velada mágica. Ahora toca pasar de Canadá a Abu Dhabi, donde se celebrará el UFC 333 el próximo sábado -segundo evento numerado del mes- y habrá dos cinturones en juego y una cartelera apasionante que a priori será histórica. articles.title: Former prisoner's BKFC fight ends in 4th-round KO against full time active police officer who felt bad for his kids
articles.summary: At BKFC 95, Jimmy Rivera, a former UFC bantamweight and current police officer, scores a fourth-round knockout against Brandon Meyer, a former inmate turned fighter, leaving him apologetic for the implications of his victory on Meyer’s family.
articles.body: Jimmy Rivera’s life has taken him from the UFC’s bantamweight division to the New Jersey police force, but the former contender has continued fighting inside the ring. At BKFC 95 in Newark, Rivera faced Brandon Meyer, who spent 12 years in federal prison before pursuing combat sports, in a matchup that drew attention for the very different paths the two men had taken. Rivera ultimately won by knockout, though the finish left him apologising to Meyer’s children.Rivera and Meyer’s unusual paths brought them together at BKFC 95The matchup took place on the undercard of BKFC 95 at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey, where the promotion staged a card headlined by Jamel Herring against John Dodson for the BKFC bantamweight title. BKFC, which stages bare-knuckle contests, had recently attracted attention with a fight between former UFC stars Darren Till and Yoel Romero.Rivera, a former UFC bantamweight who faced former champions Petr Yan and Aljamain Sterling, entered the bout as a serving police officer. Meyer, meanwhile, had spent 12 years behind bars before turning to mixed martial arts and bare-knuckle fighting.Meyer’s involvement with the criminal justice system began when he was 12 and placed on juvenile probation after a friend told police he had broken into an ice machine. His stepfather was later sentenced to life in prison for murder, and Meyer himself spent more than a decade in federal prison.He eventually found his way into fighting after a brawl at a party spilled into a park, where around 50 or 60 people gathered to watch. The contrast between Rivera’s work in law enforcement and Meyer’s past came up during the weigh-in interview with Jake Noeker, when Rivera offered a line that captured the unusual nature of their contest.“He gets to beat me up and not get arrested for it, so it’s a win-win,” Rivera said.Rivera stopped Meyer with a fourth-round knockoutThe fight ended 46 seconds into the fourth round, when Rivera landed a combination of punches that sent Meyer to the canvas. The referee stepped in and waved off the contest, giving Rivera the victory.Rivera, who now holds a 4-1 record in BKFC, acknowledged the severity of the finish afterwards and said he felt especially bad because Meyer’s children were in his corner.“It's unbelievable. Thank you to Jersey, my friends, my family - everybody that came out to support me. This is a huge arena and it's packed out,” Rivera said.He then addressed the knockout and the family members who had witnessed it.“I feel really bad because his kids were in his corner and the shot I landed was a shot. I apologised to them and said sorry but I was looking for that one shot,” Rivera said.Rivera explained that he had tried to remain patient rather than force an exchange, adding: “I took my time. Surprisingly he wasn't engaging as much. I had to be patient.”From UFC contender to New Jersey police officerRivera’s fighting career once centred on the UFC, where he competed at bantamweight against some of the division’s leading names. His life changed significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic, when he began exploring work outside professional fighting.He initially tried dispatch work and later taught jiu-jitsu to police officers, before graduating from the New Jersey Police Academy in January 2023. He subsequently joined the Elmwood Park Police Department, balancing law enforcement with his work as a gym owner, instructor and BKFC fighter.The transition was not simply a change of career, Rivera told MMA Junkie, but reflected his need to stay occupied and keep working.“I won’t say I have ADHD, but I can’t stop,” he said. “I always have to work. I’ve always got to do something. I’m all about the grinding.”Rivera also spoke about the mental strain of having nothing to do, particularly after watching people struggle with retirement.“It’s also very bad mentally, to not do anything. You see people who retire and they don’t do anything. They end up getting right back into it or they mentally degrade and don’t look the best anymore,” he said.Before the pandemic, Rivera had been a UFC contender; now, he combines police work with training, teaching and competing, sometimes through 70- to 80-hour working weeks. articles.title: UFC's Dana White Jokes About Cutting Joaquin Buckley for Not Shaking His Hand in Viral Video
articles.summary: UFC president Dana White brushed off a viral video of welterweight contender Joaquin Buckley refusing to shake his hand.
articles.body:
UFC president Dana White brushed off a viral video of welterweight contender Joaquin Buckley refusing to shake his hand.

When asked about Buckley's perceived diss at Friday's weigh-ins, White joked that Buckley's second-round knockout loss to Mike Malott at Saturday's UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta, almost cost him his roster spot.

"As soon as he lost, I told Hunter to cut him," White said before adding with a laugh, "I'm f--king joking."

Buckley snubbed White's handshake as he faced off with Malott on Friday, and he followed that up by refusing to answer any questions in his pre-fight interview:

Despite Buckley's antics, White said he didn't feel disrespected because he knows every fighter handles pressure differently.

"Yes, I have no problem with Joaquin Buckley. I've been in this business for so long, you can't take any of that stuff personal," he said. "I just stay out of everybody's way. However you're dealing with fight week is your business and your deal. It's all good."
